Samuelem quoque & Malachim, id est, quatuor regum libros. Idem lib. 2. ad Rufinum, cap. 7. In libris quoque Samuelis & Malachim, quos nos regnorum quatuor nominamus, post catalogum divinae scripturae haec intuli, &c.
units.tr: The Books of Kings follow] four in number, of which the first two are assigned in the Hebrew liturgical books to Samuel, and the latter are inscribed with the name of Kings. Note that all these books in Greek manuscripts have the title βασιλειῶν [of kingdoms], that is, of kingdoms; hence shortly after, Eli the priest is said to belong to the books of kingdoms. Jerome, letter [number illegible]: "Samuel also and Malachim, that is, the four books of Kings." The same, to Rufinus, bk. 2, ch. 7: "In the books also of Samuel and Malachim, which we call the four books of Kingdoms, after the list of divine Scripture I have added these things," etc.

units.la: Pag. 50. Libris regnorum] id est, Mamlachoth. Rursum Hiero. praefatione in libros regum, meliusque multo est Malachim, id est, regum, quam Malachoth, id est, regnorum dicere. Non enim multarum gentium discribit regna, sed unius Israelitici populi, qui tribubus duodecim continetur. Locus iste censura indiget. Nam non memini legere usquam Malachoth hoc significatu. Quid igitur? Regnum Ebraice Melucha dicitur & Mamlacha, unde pluralis Mamlachoth, non Malachoth: quod potius opera denotat a singulari מלאכה[?] Melacha sive Malacha, opus; cuius thema Laach, non Malach, regna vit.
units.tr: p. 50. The books of Kingdoms] that is, Mamlachoth. Again Jerome, in the preface to the books of Kings, says that "Malachim, that is, of kings, is much better than Malachoth, that is, of kingdoms." For it does not describe the kingdoms of many nations, but of the one Israelite people, which is contained in twelve tribes. That passage needs correction, for I do not remember reading Malachoth anywhere in this sense. What then? In Hebrew the word for kingdom is Melucha and Mamlacha, whence the plural is Mamlachoth, not Malachoth; this rather denotes work, from the singular מלאכה [melacha], that is, Melacha or Malacha, work; whose root is Laach, not Malach, to reign.

units.la: Anni CCCC. & XIX.] ita Gifelinus olim hunc locum correxit. Prius erat CCCC. & IX, qui numerus proxime accedit ad eum, qui habetur. Act. 13.20. μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις[?] καὶ πεντήκοντα. Nam Eli sacerdos inter judices numeratur. Is judicatum administravit annos quadraginta, ut habetur 1 Sam. 4.18. Quanquam Sulpitiũ tantum viginti annos ei attributat: ex cujus supputatione Sigonius hoc loco reposuit CCC. & XXXIX. Sed ex subjecta tabula tantum colliguntur CCC. & IX. Othoniel praefuit ann. | 50. secundum Ebraeos 40. Ahod | 80. Semigar | 1. Debbora | 40. Gedeon | 40. Abimelech | 3. Thola | 22. Iair | 22. Iephthe | 6. Ebefon | 7. Ailon | 10. Abdon quem Eusebius Labdon vocat. | 8. Samson | 20. Summa | 309.
units.tr: Years 419] Gifelinus once corrected this place thus. Previously it was 409, a number that comes closest to the one given, Acts 13:20: "after these things, about four hundred and fifty years." For Eli the priest is counted among the judges. He administered judgment for forty years, as is found in 1 Sam. 4:18. Although Sulpicius attributes only twenty years to him, from whose calculation Sigonius restored here 339. But from the table below only 309 can be gathered. Othniel presided for 50 years, according to the Hebrews 40. Ehud 80. Shamgar 1. Deborah 40. Gideon 40. Abimelech 3. Tola 22. Jair 22. Jephthah 6. Ibzan 7. Elon 10. Abdon, whom Eusebius calls Labdon. 8. Samson 20. Total 309.

units.la: His adde annos tyrannidis, quos Ebraei superioribus inclusos arbitrantur. Chufan rasathaim | 8. Eglon | 18. Iabin | 20. Madian | 7. Philisthaei sive Allophyli | 18. Rursum Philistaei | 40. Summa | 111.
units.tr: To these add the years of tyranny, which the Hebrews think are included in the years above. Cushan-rishathaim 8. Eglon 18. Jabin 20. Midian 7. Philistines or Allophyli 18. Again the Philistines 40. Total 111.

units.la: Ex his concludo, si annis Iudicum annumeraveris annos tyrannidis, Othonielique tantum 40. attribueris, conflari annos CCCC. & IX. vel potius X. Sic etiam se tuetur numerus qui Act. 13. in libris vulgatis. Sed de hoc alias.
units.tr: From these I conclude that if you count the years of tyranny among the years of the judges, and attribute only forty to Othniel, the total comes to 409 or rather 410. In this way too the number in Acts 13 in the printed editions is upheld. But of this elsewhere.

units.la: A mundi autem exordio ann. IIIIM. CCC. & III. ] hunc numerum conficit Gifelinus [?] ex his duobus locis. Pag. 40. scribit a mundi exordio usque ad excessum Iosue annos esse IIIM. DCCC. LXXX. & IIII. Hic vero scribit a die mortis Iosue in id tempus quo Samson defunctus est numerari annos CCCC. & XIX. Simul hi numeri efficiunt. 4303. Sigonius vero, qui superiori numero adjecerat viginti, hunc ita emendat, ut pro 3. reponat 23.
units.tr: From the beginning of the world, however, 4,323 years] Gifelinus makes this number from these two places. On p. 40 he writes that from the beginning of the world to the death of Joshua there were 3,880 years. Here, however, he writes that from the day of Joshua's death to the time when Samson died 419 years are counted. Together these numbers make 4303. Sigonius, however, who had added twenty to the former number, corrects this so that for 3 he puts 23.

units.la: Non incuriose latentem, &c. ] Sic infra, quae non incuriose a nobis sunt digesta.
units.tr: Not carelessly hidden, etc.] So below, things which we have not carelessly arranged.

units.la: Heli sacerdos] Eli septimus erat ab Aharone, ab Ithamaro ejus filio altero genus ducens. Fuit autem, ut Iosephus refert, pontifex ex hac familia primus, cujus genus in pontificatu mansit usque ad Salomonis tempora, quando ad Eleazari familiam rursum rediit. Ant. hist. lib. 5. cap. 12.
units.tr: Eli the priest] Eli was the seventh from Aaron, tracing his descent from Ithamar, Aaron's second son. He was, as Josephus reports, the first high priest from this family, whose line remained in the priesthood until the times of Solomon, when it returned again to the family of Eleazar. Jewish Antiquities, bk. 5, ch. 12.

units.la: Samuel] Levites & propheta.
units.tr: Samuel] a Levite and prophet.

units.la: Elchana] malim Elcana. Sic enim & Graeci scribunt Ἐλκανά[?], Genus ducebat ab Elcana filio Core, ac propterea creditur etiam propheta fuisse. Nam filij Core prophetae erant. Rei firmandae quod 1. Sam. 1. 1. ex Ramathaim Sophim, si modo ibi Sophim, ut quidam opinantur, significat speculatores, id est, prophetas. Videndus R. David, quem Camium cognominant.
units.tr: Elkanah] I prefer Elcana. For the Greeks also write Ἐλκανά [Elkana]. He traced his descent from Elcanah, son of Korah, and therefore he is believed also to have been a prophet, for the sons of Korah were prophets. To confirm this, [note] 1 Sam. 1:1, "from Ramathaim Zophim," if indeed Zophim here, as some think, means watchmen, that is, prophets. R. David should be consulted, whom they nickname Kimchi.

units.la: Anna] scribe Hanna cum aspiratione, id est, חנה[?] Sic vocabatur etiam mater septem fratrum Machabaeorum, quorum histo-riam Iosephus descripsit peculiari libro, qui περὶ τῆς αὐτοκράτορος λογισμοῦ[?] inscribitur. Antiqui μακκαβαικοί[?] appellant.
units.tr: Anna] write Hannah with the aspirate, that is, חנה [Hannah]. The mother of the seven Maccabean brothers was also called this, whose history Josephus described in a special book, which is inscribed "On the Sovereignty of Reason" [περὶ τῆς αὐτοκράτορος λογισμοῦ]. The ancients call them the Maccabees.

units.la: Cum adolevisset] 1. Sam. 2. 26. exacto anno duodecimo ætatis. Iosephus.
units.tr: When he had grown up] 1 Sam. 2:26, after the twelfth year of his age had passed. Josephus.

units.la: Iram denuncians] iram Dei, poenam divinam.
units.tr: Announcing wrath] the wrath of God, the divine punishment.

units.la: Ob vitam filiorum] Ophni & Phinees
units.tr: On account of the life of his sons] Hophni and Phinehas.

units.la: Pag 51 Munera a sacrificantibus exigentes] non hoc tantum faciebant, sed etiam mulierum religionis causa eo ad sacrum locum confluentium pudicitiam expugnabant.
units.tr: p. 51. Exacting gifts from those who sacrificed] They not only did this, but also violated the chastity of women who came together to the holy place for the sake of worship.

units.la: Sed levior objurgatio] Hieronymus, Eli pro iniquitate filiorum suorum damnatus est. Corripuit quidem eos, sed lenitate patris non autoritate pontificis: & quia eos tenebatur corripere, ideo non solum pro iniquitate filiorum, sed etiam pro sua fuit punitus.
units.tr: But a milder rebuke] Jerome: Eli was condemned for the wickedness of his sons. He indeed rebuked them, but with a father's gentleness rather than with the authority of a high priest; and because he was bound to correct them, he was punished not only for the wickedness of his sons but also for his own.

units.la: Sed victi Hebraei] caesa sunt in hoc praelio circiter quatuor millia, 1. Sam. 4. 2.
units.tr: But the Hebrews were defeated] about four thousand were slain in this battle, 1 Sam. 4:2.

units.la: Cum ea filij sacerdotis prodeunt] addit Iosephus accepisse a patre mandatum, si amissa arca vivere sustinerent, ne unquam in conspectum suum venirent.
units.tr: When the sons of the priest went forth with it] Josephus adds that they had received a command from their father that, if they were willing to live after the loss of the ark, they should never come into his sight.

units.la: Annis gravior] agebat tum annum aetatis octavum supra nonagesimum.
units.tr: Heavier with years] he was then in the ninety-eighth year of his age.

units.la: Luminibus obductis] oculis caligantibus, 1. Sam. 4. 15.
units.tr: With eyes dimmed] with eyes growing dim, 1 Sam. 4:15.

units.la: Praesentis Domini] id est, arcae. Sic, venit Deus in castra.
units.tr: Of the present Lord] that is, of the ark. Thus, "God has come into the camp."

units.la: Nam symbolum erat divinitatis in terra.
units.tr: For it was a sign of the divinity on earth.

units.la: Fugam parabant] fugam parasse non legitur in Scriptura. duntaxat scriptum ibi est eos in magno metu fuisse ob præsen-tiam arcæ.
units.tr: They were preparing flight. Scripture does not say that they had prepared flight. It says only that they were in great fear because of the presence of the ark.

units.la: Non sine Domino] non sine divina providentia.
units.tr: Not without the Lord means not without divine providence.

units.la: Victi Hebræi, arca capitur] ceciderunt in hac pugna triginta millia peditum, 1 Sam. 4.10.
units.tr: The Hebrews were defeated and the ark was captured. Thirty thousand foot soldiers fell in this battle, 1 Sam. 4.10.

units.la: Animam expiravit] de sella in dorsum delapsus cervicem fregit.
units.tr: He breathed his last. Having slipped from his seat onto his back, he broke his neck.

units.la: Per annos viginti] in editione Romana, ἐτῶν κ ἔτη. Ita est in LL.AA. & sic Eusebius in Chronicis affirmat scripsisse LXX. interpretes. Ceterum in vulgatis editionibus Græcis, itemque in Ebræa est τεσσαρακοντα, id est, quadraginta. Sunt etiam qui putant errorem hunc natum ex affinitate litterarum μ & κ: quarum hæc in numeris denotat 20, illa vero 40.
units.tr: For twenty years. In the Roman edition the Greek reads ἐτῶν κ, ἔτη [twenty years]. So it is in the LL.AA., and Eusebius in the Chronicle affirms that the Seventy translators wrote it so. But in the common Greek editions, and in the Hebrew, it is τεσσαρακοντα, that is, forty. Some also think this error arose from the resemblance of the letters μ and κ, of which the latter (kappa) stands for 20 in numerals and the former (mu) for 40.

units.la: Sacerdotium administravit] & judicatum. Nam simul & sacerdos erat & judex. Sane in fonte, judicavit Israelem, &c. Sacerdotium autem posuit pro pontificatu, ut supra pag. 50, qui sacerdotium patris in quæstum verterant. Sic ἱερωσύνη pro ἀρχιερωσύνη in libris Machabæorum.
units.tr: He administered the priesthood and judged. For he was at once both priest and judge. Indeed, in the source, "he judged Israel," etc. But he put "priesthood" for high priesthood, as above on p. 50, where men had turned their father's priesthood into profit. So ἱερωσύνη [hierōsynē] is used for ἀρχιερωσύνη [archierōsynē] in the books of the Maccabees.

units.la: Eorum opido Azoto Ἀζωτος quasi Asdodus, aut ab Azza uxore conditoris appellata. Asdod antiquum urbis nomen, quam posterior ætas Palmum dixit. Autor Benjamin in Itinerario suo. Hæc urbs obsessa fuit olim a Psammiticho-rege Ægypti annos undetriginta continuos. Proinde scribit Herodotus lib. 2. αὐτη δὲ ἡ πόλις Ἄζωτος ἀπὸ πολλῶν ἐτῶν.
units.tr: Their town Azotus [Ἀζωτος], as if Asdodus, or named after Azza, the wife of its founder. Asdod was the ancient name of the city, which a later age called Palmus. The author is Benjamin in his Itinerary. This city was once besieged for twenty-nine continuous years by Psammitichus, king of Egypt. Hence Herodotus writes in book 2: "But this city, Azotus, for many years" [αὐτὴ δὲ ἡ πόλις Ἄζωτος ἀπὸ πολλῶν ἐτῶν].

units.la: Dagon] vide commentarium ad pag. 4 8. Piscis formam habuisse testatur R. Salomo. Sed & Nicolaus de Lyra, R. David, Ajunt Dagon ab umbelico & infra piscem retulisse, supra umbelicum speciem hominis habuisse. Quo accommodant illud, tantum Dagon remansisse in eo, quod interpretantur, quod referebat piscem: alii melius, truncus Dagon. Græci fabulantur hunc esse unum ex quatuor filiis Urani, quos ex Ge, id est, terra suscepit. Dicunt etiam invenisse frumentum, quod Dagon dicitur, unde Dagon quasi Σιτών, & aratrum, unde ζωοτροφὸς dictus. Eusebius in libris Περὶ ὀνομάτων, pag. 23. & sequente 24.
units.tr: Dagon: see the commentary on p. 48. R. Solomon testifies that it had the form of a fish. But Nicolas de Lyra and R. David also say that Dagon was like a fish from the navel down, and above the navel had the appearance of a man. To this they fit the statement that only what they interpret as representing a fish remained of Dagon; others, better, say "the trunk of Dagon." The Greeks fable that he was one of the four sons of Uranus whom Ge, that is the earth, received. They also say that he discovered grain, which is called dagan, whence Dagon as if Sitōn [Σιτών], and the plough, whence he was called zōotrophos [ζωοτροφὸς]. See Eusebius, On Names [Περὶ ὀνομάτων], p. 23 and the following p. 24.

units.la: Simulachrum dæmoni dicatum] nam dij gentium dæmonia, ut quidem Græca ecclesia legit apud David. Sane dia-bolus bolus in Iovis aut Mercurij forma sæpe apparuit. Sulpicius in vita Martini, segm.14. Frequenter autem diabolus visibilem se ei formis diversissimis offerebat. Nam interdum in Iovis personam, plerumque Mercurij, persæpe etiam se Veneris ac Minervæ transfiguratum vultibus offerebat.
units.tr: An image dedicated to a demon: for the gods of the nations are demons, as the Greek Church reads in David. The devil often appeared in the form of Jove or Mercury. Sulpicius, in the Life of Martin, section 14. The devil frequently offered himself to him visibly in the most diverse forms. For at times he offered himself in the person of Jove, more often of Mercury, and very often transformed into the faces of Venus and Minerva.

units.la: Dicatum] alibi dedicatum, ut in vita Martini, segm.10. arborem illam excidi oportere, quod esset dæmoni dedicata.
units.tr: Dedicated. Elsewhere "dedicated," as in the Life of Martin, section 10: that the tree had to be cut down because it was dedicated to a demon.

units.la: Diicerptum est] caput & manus abscisse a reliquo trunco. Quod pro iis facit qui humana specie Dagonem effinguni. Nam pisces non habent manus. Sunt qui tradant (id supra probatum est) superiore parte corporis hominem, inferiore piscem fuisse, hoc est piscis speciem & formam habuisse. Cujusmodi sunt poetarum scriptis nobilitati Tritones. Qualem descripsit Virgilius, cum ita caneret,
units.tr: Torn to pieces: the head and hands were cut off from the rest of the trunk. This favours those who shape Dagon in human form, for fish have no hands. There are those who hold (this was proved above) that the upper part of the body was human and the lower part a fish, that is, that he had the appearance and form of a fish. Such are the Tritons made famous in the writings of the poets, as Virgil described them when he sang:

units.la: Frons hominem præfert, in pristin definit alvus.
units.tr: The front shows a man, but the belly ends in a fish.

units.la: Sed vide sis Quæstiones meas.
units.tr: But please see my Questions.

units.la: Inde mures per omnem regionem exorti] 1. Sam. 5. in editione LXX. [illegible, ~24 letters] Rursum cap. 6. [illegible, ~30 letters] lib. 6. cap 1. [illegible, ~45 letters] Quæ sic versa repperi, Ager vero totus scatebat muribus, quia omnia vastantes nec segetibus parcebant nec ceteris fru-ctibus[?].
units.tr: Then mice arose throughout the whole region. 1 Sam. 5 in the LXX edition [illegible, about 24 letters]. Again ch. 6 [illegible, about 30 letters]; book 6, ch. 1 [illegible, about 45 letters]. Which I found translated thus: "And the whole field swarmed with mice, because they ravaged everything and spared neither the crops nor the other fruits."

units.la: Pag. 52. Multa hominum millia letho dabant] in eadem editione, καὶ ἐγένετο σύγχυσις θάνατος μεγάλη ἐν τῇ πόλει. [illegible, ~5 letters] interpretantur σύγχυσις θάνατος.
units.tr: P. 52. They gave many thousands of men to death. In the same edition: καὶ ἐγένετο σύγχυσις θάνατος μεγάλη ἐν τῇ πόλει [and there was a great confusion, a death, in the city]. [illegible, about 5 letters] they render it σύγχυσις θάνατος [confusion, death].

units.la: Arcam Dei ad Gethæos translulerunt] 1. Sam. 5.7. eadem editio habet καὶ λέγουσιν οἱ γιγενη[?]οι, ἀπέστειλαν τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ θεοῦ [?] ἡμᾶς, καὶ μετέλαβεν κιβωτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ Ἰσραὴλ εἰς γῆν[?]. Latina vero, & responderunt Gethæi, circumducatur arca Dei Israel. Et circumduxerunt arcam Dei Israel, nempe per omnes urbes Philistæorum. Quod etiam Iosephus annotavit ita scribens, atque in hunc modum per quinque Palæstinorum urbes pervagata ait[?] arca, veluti tributum per singulas pœnas violatæ religionis exigens. lib. 6. cap. 1.
units.tr: They carried the ark of God to the Gittites. 1 Sam. 5.7. The same edition has καὶ λέγουσιν οἱ γιγενη…, ἀπέστειλαν τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ θεοῦ … ἡμᾶς, καὶ μετέλαβεν κιβωτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ Ἰσραὴλ εἰς γῆν…. The Latin, however, reads: "And they answered, let the ark of the God of Israel be carried about." And they carried the ark of the God of Israel about, namely through all the cities of the Philistines. Josephus also noted this, writing thus: "And in this manner the ark, passing through five cities of the Palestinians, exacted as it were a tribute from each for the penalties of violated religion." Book 6, ch. 1.

units.la: In opidum Ascalonensium] εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα, id est, Ascalo-nem. Sic Græci codices. Sed Latini, ut & Ebræi, in Accaron. Utrumque oppidum erat Palæstinæ proprie dictæ.
units.tr: Into the town of the Ascalonites [εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα], that is, Ascalon. So the Greek codices; but the Latin, like the Hebrews, has Accaron. Both towns belonged to Palestine properly so called.

units.la: Gentis ejus primoribus] Philisthæorum satrapis.
units.tr: To the leading men of that nation the satraps of the Philistines.

units.la: Ex sententia principū,&c.]LXX. ἀγὼ καλέσαι Ἀλλόφυλοι τοὺς ἱερεῖς καὶ τοὺς μάντεις καὶ τοὺς ἐπῳδοὺς ἀνδρας [?], id est, sa-cerdotes, vates & incantatores suos. Latina vetus vocaverunt sacerdotes & divinos. Sic etiam Ebraei.
units.tr: According to the decision of the princes, etc. LXX: [ἀγὼ καλέσαι Ἀλλόφυλοι τοὺς ἱερεῖς καὶ τοὺς μάντεις καὶ τοὺς ἐπῳδοὺς ἀνδρας], that is, their priests, prophets and enchanters. The old Latin has "they called priests and diviners." So also the Hebrews.

units.la: Multis cum muneribus] munera erant, quinque ani [?] aurei, totidemque mures aurei, 1.Sam.6.5.
units.tr: With many gifts. The gifts were five golden tumours and as many golden mice, 1 Sam. 6.5.

units.la: Remittitur] cum fuisset in agro Philisthæorum septem menses, 1.Sam.6.1. Nam quod in Iosepho μῆνας τετρᾶς [?] emendandum est ex hoc loco, maxime cum in Rufino fit, mensibus septem,id est, μῆνας ἑπτά.
units.tr: Released. When it had been in the land of the Philistines for seven months, 1 Sam. 6.1. For the reading μῆνας τετρᾶς [four months] in Josephus must be corrected from this passage, especially since in Rufinus it is "seven months," that is μῆνας ἑπτά.

units.la: Ex opido Beth-samis] imo ex agro ubi triticum metebant.
units.tr: From the town of Beth-shemesh: indeed from the field where they were reaping wheat.

units.la: Bethsamis] melius, Bethsames. ישמש [?] Sames,ut בית שמש [?] Ha-bel. In edit. Romana Βαιθσάμυς [?], quod scribes Baithsamys, vel certe Baeth samys. Opidum hoc situm erat in termino tribus Iudæ Iof.15.10. Quod firmabis alio loco qui habetur, 2.Reg.14.11. in Bethsames opido Iudæ.
units.tr: Bethshemesh: better, Bethshames. Hebrew [שמש] Shames, as in [בית שמש] Beth-shemesh. In the Roman edition Βαιθσάμυς [Baithsamys], which one should write Baithsamys or certainly Baeth samys. This town lay on the border of the tribe of Judah, Josh. 15.10. Which you will confirm from another passage, 2 Kings 14.11, in the town of Bethshames in Judah.

units.la: Mox Levitæ] hoc Bethsamithæ fecisse leguntur, 1.Sam.6.15. & ideo puniti fuerunt. Iosephus lib.6 [?]. cap.2.
units.tr: Soon the Levites. It is read that these men of Beth-shemesh did this, 1 Sam. 6.15, and therefore they were punished. Josephus, book 6, ch. 2.

units.la: Quorum hoc negotium erat] imo negotium hoc erat sacerdotum, non levitarum. Verum nostler [?] hæc nomina confundere videtur. Videnotata ad paginam proxime sequentem.
units.tr: Whose business this was. Indeed this business belonged to the priests, not the Levites. But our author seems to confuse these names. See the notes on the next page.

units.la: Per totam urbem sævitum] ob attractatam arcam ab hominibus profanis.
units.tr: Throughout the whole town there was slaughter on account of the ark being handled by profane men.

units.la: Pag.53. Samuel sacerdos] Iudex erat, prophetes & levita. Etiamne sacerdos? Si sacerdotis vocabulum stricte accipiatur pro pontifice verum non est. Nam τῷ Ἠλὶ [?] Eli successit in pontificatu Achitob. Neque vero late sumptum verum esse potest, cum non fuerit ex posteris Aharon, qui soli sacerdotes dicebantur. At obtulit holocaustum? Quid tum posteat? Nam idem Gedeon fecisse memoratur. Dicendum igitur nomen sacerdotis hic sumi latissime, ut etiam levitas comprehendat. Supra pag.33. igitur Levi tribu in sacerdotium segregata: & pag.38. Levitis in sacerdotium assumptis Sic infra pag.61. Samuel admodum senex sacerdotio functus. Huc retulerim quod pag.34. quod erat netas (loquitur de tabernaculo) nisi sacerdotibus introire. Firmabo nunc, quæ dixi, auctoritate Hieronymi. Adversus Vigilantium,cap.2. Samuel & levita & prophetes fuit. Contra Helvidium lib.1. cap.13. Simulque noxcendum quod Samuel Samuel Levita, non sacerdos, non pontifex fuerit. Unde & faciebat illi mater sua Ephod bad, superhumerale videlicet lineum, qui habitus proprie Levitarum & minoris est ordinis. Unde & in Psalmis non nominatur inter sacerdotes, sed inter eos qui invocant nomé Domini, Moyses, inquit, & Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus, & Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus. Levi enim genuit Caath, Caath genuit Aminadab, Aminadab genuit Chore, Chore genuit Afsir, Afsir genuit Elchana, Elchana genuit Sub, Sub genuit Tou, Tou genuit Eliu, Eliu genuit Ieroam, Ieroam genuit Elchana, Elchana genuit Samuelem.
units.tr: P. 53. Samuel the priest. He was a judge, prophet and Levite. Was he also a priest? If the word "priest" is taken strictly for high priest, it is not true; for Ahitub succeeded Eli in the high priesthood. Nor can it be true if taken broadly, since he was not of the descendants of Aaron, who alone were called priests. But did he offer a burnt offering? What follows from that? For Gideon is also recorded as having done the same. It must therefore be said that the name of priest is taken here very broadly, so as to include Levites too. Above, on p. 33, the tribe of Levi had been set apart for the priesthood; and on p. 38, the Levites were admitted to the priesthood. So below, on p. 61, Samuel, very old, served as priest. To this I would refer what is said on p. 34, that the tabernacle, which was a net, was entered only by priests (he is speaking of the tabernacle). I will now confirm what I have said by the authority of Jerome. Against Vigilantius, ch. 2: Samuel was both Levite and prophet. Against Helvidius, book 1, ch. 13: at the same time it should be noted that Samuel was a Levite, not a priest, not a high priest. Hence his mother made him an ephod bad, that is, a linen ephod, a garment properly of the Levites and of a lower order. Hence too in the Psalms he is not named among the priests, but among those who call upon the name of the Lord: "Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his name," Ps. 99.6. Levi begat Kohath, Kohath begat Amram, Amram begat Izhar, Izhar begat Elkanah, Elkanah begat Zuph, Zuph begat Tohu, Tohu begat Eliab, Eliab begat Jeroham, Jeroham begat Elkanah, Elkanah begat Samuel.

units.la: An quia regale unguentum dici non potest cum nulli adhuc reges essent? Aut appellat sacerdotale quia ejusdem erat cum altero generis. Prius verius videtur. Nam ut demus ejusdem generis su-isse hoc cum illo, tamen quum eo futurus rex ungeretur, regale potius erat appellandum quam sacerdotale. David Camius negat Saulem fuisse unctum oleo unctionis, quod adhibitum duntaxat ait in familia David. Idem annotat litum fuisse oleo balsamino, quod [illegible, ~6 letters] vocant. Scribit eadem fere autor libri qui IOD[?] per sigla vocatur. Nam ait sol.191. col.4. Oleo unctionis postea ungebantur qui ex domo David: reges autem Israel balsamo ungebantur, hoc est oleo balsaminino. ticula olei est vasculum factum ex auro vel argento ad reponendum oleum unctionis, unde inungebantur reges & pontifices. Etiam e cornu perfundebantur. In scholiis Ebraeorum, Dicunt doctores, Saul & Iehu uncti fuerunt e lenticula, non fuit diuturnum regnum eorum: David & Salomo uncti fuerunt e cornu, fuit diuturnum regnum eorum. Videndus R. David loco citato.
units.tr: Or is it because "royal ointment" cannot be said when there were as yet no kings? Or is it called priestly because it was of the same kind as the other? The former seems truer. For even granting that this was of the same kind as that, yet since a future king was anointed with it, it should rather be called royal than priestly. David Kimchi denies that Saul was anointed with the oil of anointing, which he says was used only in David's family. The same writer notes that he was smeared with balsam oil, which they call [illegible, about 6 letters]. The author of the book which is cited by the sigla IOD writes almost the same thing; for he says (sol. 191, col. 4): "Afterwards those from David's house were anointed with the oil of anointing, but the kings of Israel were anointed with balsam, that is, with balsam oil." A small flask of oil is a little vessel made of gold or silver for holding the anointing oil, from which kings and high priests were anointed. They were also poured over from a horn. In the scholia of the Hebrews the teachers say: Saul and Jehu were anointed from a flask; their reign was not lasting. David and Solomon were anointed from a horn; their reign was lasting. See R. David in the passage cited.

units.la: Modestus animi formaque excellenti erat] ἀγαθὸς[?] tam ad animum refert quam ad corpus. Alij ad corpus tantum refe-runt interpretantes, pulcher, formosus.
units.tr: He was modest of mind and of outstanding appearance] [agathos?] refers to the mind as much as to the body. Others refer it to the body only, rendering it "handsome, comely".

units.la: Aliquanta ab eo pars populi desciverat] hæc paullo aliter narrantur, 1. Sam. 10.27. & 11. 1. Vide, si vacas.
units.tr: A considerable part of the people had deserted him] These things are told somewhat differently at 1 Sam. 10.27 and 11.1. See them, if you have leisure.

units.la: Seque Ammonitis conjunxerant] viri Iabes Galaad hoc in animo habebant, nisi duris conditionibus, quas eis proponebat Nahas Ammonites, deterriti fuissent.
units.tr: And had joined themselves to the Ammonites] The men of Jabesh Gilead had this in mind, but they were deterred by the harsh conditions which Nahash the Ammonite proposed to them.

units.la: Hos] Ammonitas.
units.tr: These] The Ammonites.

units.la: Iterato a Samuele unctus traditur] prius in Maspha, nunc in Galgalis.
units.tr: He is said to have been anointed a second time by Samuel] Earlier at Mizpah, now at Gilgal.

units.la: Illicita præsumptione] sequentia docent Sulpicium in eadem sententia fuisse cum Nicolao de Lyra & aliis, qui inter peccata Saulis recensent quod holocaustum obtulerit, rem ei illicitam, eo quod sacerdos non esset. Quasi vero solis sacerdotibus li-cuerit offerre holocaustum, ac non etiam aliis, qui sacerdotes non erant. Nam ne Samuel quidem sacerdos erat ex genere Aharonis. Quod si dicas Levitam fuisse, quibus hoc quoque concessum fuerit, respondeo Gedeonem etiam holocaustum Domino obtulisse, nec propterea reprehensum fuisse. Dicunt insuper Ebrai lici-tum fuisse extraneo (sic vocant eum qui sacerdos non est) offerre in excelso יחיד[?], id est, unici: quemadmodum expositum est in fine Zebachim, hoc est ejus tractatus Thalmudici, ubi de sacrifi-ciis agitur.
units.tr: By illicit presumption] What follows shows that Sulpicius held the same view as Nicholas of Lyra and others, who count among Saul's sins that he offered a burnt offering, something unlawful for him because he was not a priest. As if only priests might offer burnt offerings, and not others who were not priests. For not even Samuel was a priest of the line of Aaron. But if you say he was a Levite, and that this too was permitted to Levites, I reply that Gideon also offered a burnt offering to the Lord, and was not for that reason rebuked. Furthermore, the Hebrews say that it was lawful for an outsider (so they call one who is not a priest) to offer on the high place [יחיד], that is, "single" or "alone", as is explained at the end of Zebachim, that is, of that Talmudic tractate where sacrifices are treated.

units.la: Ad vicem sacerdotis] usitatius est, in vicem, aut vice sa-cerdotis: quod etiam dicunt, vicem sacerdotis. Sic Plautus & alij quandoque locuti sunt.
units.tr: In place of the priest] The more usual expression is "in vicem" or "vice sacerdotis". They also say "vicem sacerdotis". Thus Plautus and others sometimes spoke.

units.la: Sera peccatum pœnitentia fatebatur] Quodnam peccatum? An quod Samuelem non fuerit operitus? plane sic videtur. Nam cum jussus esset expectare dies septem, non debuisset offerre ante vesperam diei septimi. Quo die Samuel venit, sicut promiserat: serius tamen, quia peractum tunc erat sacrificium. Vide Sam. 13. 10.
units.tr: He confessed with late repentance the sin] Which sin? Perhaps that he had not waited for Samuel? That plainly seems to be the case. For when he was bidden to wait seven days, he should not have offered before evening of the seventh day. Samuel came on that day, as he had promised, yet later, because the sacrifice had by then been completed. See 1 Sam. 13.10.

units.la: Pag.55. Plures lacrymas & latebras petiverant] suspicor Severum edidisse, lacunas (sive lacus) & latebras. Nam in editione Graeca, ἀγῶ ὀνεύβη ὁ λαὸς ἐν τοῖς σπηλαίοις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς μάνδραις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς τίτεσι, καὶ ἐν τῷ βόθρῳ, καὶ ἐν τοῖς λάκκοις. Lexicon Graeco-Lat. βόθρος, fossa, fovea, lacuna. Idem Lexicon λάκκος, lacuna, laccus, cisterna. Locus est 1 Sam. 13. 6. Cui haec mea conjectura non placet, ei per me licet ut deleto, lacrymas & legat, plures latebras petiverant.
units.tr: Page 55. They had sought out many tears and hiding places] I suspect that Severus printed pits (or pools) and hiding places. For in the Greek edition, [ἐκρύβη ὁ λαὸς ἐν τοῖς σπηλαίοις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς μάνδραις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς τρώγλαις, καὶ ἐν τῷ βόθρῳ, καὶ ἐν τοῖς λάκκοις] the people hid themselves in caves, and in sheepfolds, and in holes, and in the pit, and in the cisterns. In the Greek-Latin lexicon, [βόθρος] means ditch, pit, trench, hole. The same lexicon: [λάκκος] means pit, cistern, reservoir. The place is 1 Sam. 13.6. For anyone to whom this conjecture of mine does not appeal, I permit him to delete "tears" and read they had sought out many hiding places.

units.la: Praeter imbecillitatem animorum, &c.] haec imbecillitas animorum erat ante peccatum regis. Mirum ergo cur subjiciat, qui alienum a se Dominum delicto regis arbitrabantur.
units.tr: Besides the weakness of their spirits, etc.] This weakness of spirit existed before the king's sin. It is strange therefore why he adds it, since they thought that the Lord had been estranged from them by the king's offence.

units.la: In maxima ferramentorum inopia exercitus erat] nullus erat faber ferrarius in toto Israel: itaque cum vomer aut ligo acuendus erat eundum fuit ad Philistheos. Quod significat cum ait paullo post, neque cuiquam conscienti teli bellici, aut rustici ferramenti potestas fuerat.
units.tr: In their great lack of iron tools the army was in want] There was no iron-smith in all Israel. So when a ploughshare or mattock had to be sharpened, they had to go to the Philistines. This is what he means when he says shortly afterwards that there was no means for anyone to have a weapon of war or an agricultural iron tool.

units.la: Nutu Dei] terrore divinitus incussio.
units.tr: By God's nod] Terror inspired by God.

units.la: Rex edixisse traditur] populum temere satis jurejurando adstrinxit ac dirus devovit eum qui ante vesperam, priusquam hostes confecti essent, cibum sumeret. Hoc factum Saulis culpat Josephus: culpant expositores. Idem excusant Ionathanem. Primum quod insciens fuerit edicti paterni: deinde quod necessitate compulsus hoc fecerit.
units.tr: The king is said to have decreed] He bound the people rashly enough with an oath, and dreadfully cursed whoever should take food before evening, before the enemies had been finished off. Josephus blames this deed of Saul, and the commentators blame it too. The same writers excuse Jonathan: first, because he was ignorant of his father's edict; second, because he did it under compulsion of necessity.

units.la: Spiculo] baculo extremo quem manu ferebat.
units.tr: With the spear] The end of the staff which he carried in his hand.

units.la: Pag.56. Ex Domini ira compertum] ex silentio Domini, qui non respondit ei toto die, comperit peccatum fuisse. deinde sors Ionatham prodidit.
units.tr: Page 56. It was discovered by the anger of the Lord] From the Lord's silence, since he did not answer him all day, he discovered that the sin had been committed. Then the lot betrayed Jonathan.

units.la: Ne quid ex spoliis devictorum concupiscerent] Nam una cum spoliis etiam memoria gentis remanebat, quam delere penitus decreverat.
units.tr: That they should covet nothing from the spoils of the conquered] For along with the spoils the memory of the nation also remained, which he had decided to destroy utterly.

units.la: Capta servari] ipse regem servabat, populus autem jumenta & pecudes.
units.tr: To be kept alive as captives] He himself kept the king alive, but the people kept the cattle and the flocks.

units.la: Regali unguento] oleo unctionis. Haec unctio extendebatur in omnes ipsius posteros. Quod autem Salomo unctus fuit, id factum propter Adoniam. Sic & alij quidam uncti fuerunt propter singularem aliquam causam. Qua de re videndus liber praeceptorum major, sol 191. col. 4. ubi & de ratione ungendi reges 211. 2. Qui ungebat digito suo exprimebat χ, Graecum, quod vocant ךָ, vel certe כְּךָ, id est Chaph Graecanicum. Quæ figura est crucis Andreanæ. Chaph Græcanicum vocatur & David Camio in comment. ad Pfal. 133. ubi de unctione sacerdotis, Initio induebat eum vestibus sacerdotalibus: postea fundebat oleum super caput ejus, ungebatque eodem oleo cilia oculorum ejus in modum Chaph Græcanici.
units.tr: With royal ointment] The oil of anointing. This anointing was extended to all his descendants. That Solomon was anointed, this happened on account of Adonijah. So also some others were anointed for some singular reason. On this matter see the Greater Book of Precepts, sol. 191, col. 4, where also on the manner of anointing kings, 211.2. He who anointed with his finger traced the Greek letter chi, which they call [ךָ], or certainly [כְּךָ], that is, the Greek Chaph. This figure is St Andrew's cross. The Greek Chaph is also so called by David Camius in his commentary on Psalm 133, where, speaking of the anointing of the priest: at first he clothed him in priestly vestments; afterwards he poured oil over his head, and anointed the eyelids of his eyes with the same oil in the manner of a Greek Chaph.

units.la: Vir mirae magnitudinis ] sex cubitos & dodrantem longus.
units.tr: A man of wondrous size] Six cubits and a span tall.

units.la: Pag.57. Virga tantum] pedum erat, id est, baculus pastoralis fiue agolum. ita Festo baculus ille dicitur ab agendis pecoribus.
units.tr: Page 57. Only the staff] It was a crook, that is, a shepherd's staff or pastoral staff. So Festus calls that staff a staff for driving flocks.

units.la: Gladium postea in templum posuit] malum in templo. Sic est profecto: in tabernaculo conuentus, quod erat Nobe, posuit gladium. Reliqua arma detracta giganti posuit in tabernaculo suo, hoc est in domo sua: caput autem detulit terofolymam. Vide fis Davidem Camium, 1.Sam.17.54. Vide quoque 1.Sam 21.9.
units.tr: He afterwards put the sword in the temple] I would rather say "in the temple". So it certainly is: he put the sword in the tabernacle of assembly, which was at Nob. He put the other weapons taken from the giant in his own tabernacle, that is, in his house; but he brought the head to Jerusalem. See, if you like, David Camius on 1 Sam. 17.54. See also 1 Sam. 21.9.

units.la: Multus circa David favor] cum dicerent eum decem millia fuperasse, Saulem vero mille tantum. Hoc ei inuidiam conciliabat apud regem.
units.tr: Great favour around David] Since they said he had surpassed ten thousand, but Saul only a thousand. This won him envy with the king.

units.la: Tribunum ] chiliarchum, fiue mille militum praefectum.
units.tr: Tribune] A chiliarch, that is, commander of a thousand soldiers.

units.la: Cum ei filiam spopondisset] filiam natu majorem, Merob nomine.
units.tr: When he had betrothed her to him] The elder daughter, named Merab.

units.la: Alteri tradidit] Adrieli Molothitha.
units.tr: He gave her to another] To Adriel the Meholathite.

units.la: Melchol] μελχόλ[?]. Sed in Hiero. Michol, & in textu Ebræo, Michal, cum A breui, quod Pathach vocant, in ultima.
units.tr: Melchol] [Melchol?]. But in Jerome it is Michol, and in the Hebrew text Michal, with a short A, which they call Pathach, in the last syllable.

units.la: Amore David flagrare occoeperat] Sic veritas Ebraea, 1. Sam. 18 20. Sed & Græca editio ἠγάπησε μελχὸλ[?] ἡ θυγάτηρ Σαοὺλ τὸν Δαβίδ. Dilexit Melchol filia Saul David. Latina exemplaria variant. Nam in aliis, dilexit autem Michol filia Saul altera David: & in aliis, dilexit autem David Michol filiam Saul alteram. Virumque verum esse potest.
units.tr: Had begun to burn with love for David] So the Hebrew truth, 1 Sam. 18.20. But the Greek edition also reads: "Melchol the daughter of Saul loved David." The Latin copies vary. For in some it is "but Michol the other daughter of Saul loved David", and in others "but David loved Michol the other daughter of Saul". Both can be true.

units.la: Pag.58. Centum præputia] ἑκατὸν ἀκροβυστίας. Iosephus habet, sexcenta hostium capita.
units.tr: A hundred foreskins] [a hundred foreskins] in the Greek. Josephus has six hundred heads of enemies.

units.la: Spiritu erroris] spiritu Dei malo.
units.tr: By a spirit of error] By an evil spirit from God.

units.la: Indead Abimelech] adde, si placet, post ad regem Geth. Nam id omissum a Sulpicio.
units.tr: Then Abimelech] Add, if you like, after "to the king of Gath", for that was omitted by Sulpicius.

units.la: Abimelech] Αβιμέλεχ est in editione τῶν LXX. quam nunc secutus videtur. Ceterum in Ebræa & Latina Vulgata Achimelech legitur, ut etiam in Iosepho. Achimelech ipse patrem habuit Achitob dictum. Fuit alius Achimelech filius Abiathar memoratus, 2. Sam. 8. 20 qui Abimelech vocatur, 1. Paralip. 18. 16. scribi etiam potest Abimelech. Nam est Heth in scriptura Ebraica.
units.tr: Abimelech] [Abimelech] is in the edition of the Seventy, which he now seems to follow. But in the Hebrew and in the Latin Vulgate it is read as Achimelech, as also in Josephus. Achimelech himself had a father called Achitob. Another Achimelech is mentioned as son of Abiathar, 2 Sam. 8.20, who is called Abimelech at 1 Chron. 18.16; it can also be written Abimelech, for the Hebrew Scripture has [ח] (Heth).

units.la: Ad regem Moab] ubi parentes reliquit.
units.tr: To the king of Moab] Where he left his parents.

units.la: In terram Iudae] alibi est, Iudaeae: quod eodem recidit Nam Iudaea vocatur quandoque tribus Iuda. Quod ita notum ut probationis non indigeat.
units.tr: Into the land of Judah] Elsewhere it is Judaea, which comes to the same thing, for Judaea is sometimes called the tribe of Judah. This is so well known that it needs no proof.

units.la: Abimelech sacerdotem] Nobe degentem, ubi pontifex erat, quem Doeg Idumaeus interemit cum 85 viris Ephod lineum gestantibus. Sed vide sis, 1. Reg. 22. 19. Abimelech iste is est, quem supra in codicibus Ebraeis & Latinis Achimelech vocari diximus. Filius et Abiathar, qui solus evasit & ad Davidem transfugit.
units.tr: Abimelech the priest] Living at Nob, where he was high priest, whom Doeg the Edomite slew together with eighty-five men wearing linen ephods. But see, if you like, 1 Kings 22.19. This Abimelech is the one whom we said above is called Achimelech in the Hebrew and Latin copies. He was the son of Abiathar, who alone escaped and deserted to David.

units.la: Doeg Syrus] δωὴγ ὁ σύρος[?], quod perperam δωὴγ scriptum, & Syrus, id est, [illegible, ~5 letters] Aramaeus error lectionis. Nam in Ebraeo [illegible, ~5 letters] id est, Idumaeus. Quomodo sane Hieronymus olim legit, Iosephus Graecam lectionem secutus. Forte autem, inquit, aderat quidam servus natione Syrus, regiarum mularum curator. Antiq. lib. 6. cap 14. Error natus ex affinitate litterarum Res & Daleth, quae teste Hiero. apice duntaxat distinguuntur. An variatio fuerit aliquando in codicibus Ebraeis, nescio: hoc scio scripturam a lectione variare in his vocibus, 4. Reg. 16. 6. Nam scriptum [illegible, ~3 letters] per Res, & lectum [illegible, ~3 letters] per Daleth. Scripturam expressit interpres Chaldaeus, ut lectionem nostrer[?] Hieronymus.
units.tr: Doeg the Syrian] [Doeg ho Syros], which is wrongly written, and "Syrian", that is, Aramaean, is an error of reading. For in the Hebrew the word means Idumaean. Jerome once read it this way, and Josephus followed the Greek reading: "Perhaps," he says, "there was present a certain servant of Syrian nation, overseer of the royal mules." Antiquities, book 6, chapter 14. The error arose from the similarity of the letters Resh and Daleth, which, according to Jerome, are distinguished only by a small mark above. Whether there was ever variation in the Hebrew manuscripts I do not know; this I do know, that the writing varies from the reading in these words at 2 Kings 16.6, for one is written with Resh and read with Daleth. The Chaldee interpreter followed the written form, as our Jerome followed the reading.

units.la: Pag. 59. Desertum petiit] deserium Engaddi, 1 Sam. 24. 2.
units.tr: Page 59. He went into the wilderness] the wilderness of Engedi, 1 Sam. 24. 2.

units.la: Reficiendi corporis gratia] παρασκευάσασθαι[?], quod in editione Graeca, vertit, refugere corpus: vulgata lexica exponunt, purgare ventrem. Quod sumptum ex Hieronymo, qui tamen non Graeca, sed Ebraea transtulit. H. Stephanus in Thesauro suo conjicit legendum ἀναξυνάσασθαι[?] Id Aquila dixit ἀναξυνάσαι[?]. In Ebraeo est, tegere pedes: de quo aliquid Quaest lib. 1. quaest 35.
units.tr: For the refreshing of the body] [parasceuasasthai?], which the Greek edition renders "to ease the body"; the common lexicons explain it as "to purge the bowels." This is taken from Jerome, who however translated not from the Greek but from the Hebrew. H. Stephanus in his Thesaurus conjectures that the word should be read [anaxynasasthai?]. Aquila rendered it [anaxynasai?]. In the Hebrew it means "to cover the feet," on which see something in Quaest. book 1, question 35.

units.la: Utique[?] somno captus requiescebat] mirum unde hoc hauserit. Nam non habetur in fonte sacro.
units.tr: Somehow, captured by sleep, he was resting] It is strange where he drew this from, for it is not found in the sacred source.

units.la: Diploidem] oram diploidis, quod Graeci dicunt [illegible, ~12 letters] Hieronymus, oram chlamydis.
units.tr: The hem of the diploid] the border of the diploid, which the Greeks call [illegible]; Jerome, the border of the cloak.

units.la: Abstulit] abscidit.
units.tr: He cut off] cut off.

units.la: Praesenti tempore] cum in spelunca alvum exoneraret.
units.tr: At that very time] while he was relieving himself in the cave.

units.la: Regem eum appellans] non regem eum appellabat, sed detebat[?], nunc scio quod certissime regnaturus sis & habituru[?] rus in manu tua regnum Israel. 1. Sam 24. 21.
units.tr: Calling him king] He was not calling him king, but ... now I know that you will most certainly reign and will hold the kingdom of Israel in your hand. 1 Sam. 24. 21.

units.la: Penitius] in Coloniensi est, penitus,
units.tr: Penitius] In the Cologne edition it is penitus.

units.la: Intra eremum] intra desertum Pharan.
units.tr: Within the wilderness] within the wilderness of Paran.

units.la: Pag.60. Faltim cuidam] vocatur Phalti filius Lais ex Gallim, 1. Sam.25.45. Quae corrupta fede apud Iosephum in textu Graeco. Editio Romana Bibliorum Φαλτὶ habet, cetera Φαλ-τὶ. Faltim autem est ex Φαλτὶ [?], quod in locum Φαλτὶ [?] irrepsit librariorum vitio. Qualia sunt Λευί [?] & σαβί [?]. Nam veritas lectionis Λευί & σαοί [?].
units.tr: Page 60. Phaltiel, a certain man] he is called Phalti the son of Laish of Gallim, 1 Sam. 25. 44. This corrupt reading is found in Josephus' Greek text. The Roman edition of the Bibles has [Phalti], the rest [Phal-ti]. Faltim, however, comes from [Phalti?], which crept into the place of [Phalti?] through the fault of scribes. Such errors are [Levi?] and [sabi?]; for the true reading is [Levi] and [saoi?].

units.la: Ad Allophylos] ad Achis regem Geth.
units.tr: To the Allophyles] to Achish, king of Gath.

units.la: Ea tempestate Samuel diem functus est] Salmanticensis Iudaeus, obiit anno mundi 882. supra ter millesimum, vigesimo octavo mensis Iiar in Rama. Haec & supra notavimus. Rursum Salmanticensis, dixerunt doctores nostri, quorum fausta sit memoria, Samuel & Saul mortui sunt eodem anno: & mox, Samuel decessit quatuor mensibus ante Saulem. Et post aliquanto, Videtur quod Samuel egerit annum trigesimum octavum cum diem suum obiret Eli sa-cerdos. Vide sequentia.
units.tr: About that time Samuel died] The Salmanticensis, a Jew, says he died in the year of the world 882 after the three-thousandth, on the twenty-eighth day of the month Iyyar, in Ramah. We noted this above too. Again the Salmanticensis: our teachers, of blessed memory, said that Samuel and Saul died in the same year; and soon after, that Samuel died four months before Saul. And a little later: it seems that Samuel lived to the thirty-eighth year when Eli the priest died. See what follows.

units.la: Per mulierem, cuius viscera spiritus erroris impleverat circum loquitur ἐγγαστρίμυθον, i. in ventre loquentem: quam, qui Hebraea in Latinum sermonem transtulerunt, Pythonissam appellant.
units.tr: Through a woman in whom the spirit of error had filled her entrails] he speaks of her as [engastrimython], i.e. speaking in the belly; those who translated the Hebrew into Latin call her the Pythoness.

units.la: Samuelem] daemonem in specie Samuelis, quem Scriptura Samuelem appellat eo modo loquendi quo angelos vocat homines aut viros, & Raphael in historia Tobiae vocatur Azarias filius Ananiae; aut ipsum Samuelem, quem Deus permisit excitari ut futura praediceret regi quondam suo. Qui hanc opinionem tuentur in duas sententias abeunt. Nonnulli animam ipsius excitatam putant: alij corpus tantum. Quae magiae species necromantia nominatur, quando videlicet per mortuos divinamus posteriora praedicimus. Qua de re consulendus praeter Nicolaum, Paulus episcopus Burgensis, in Addit. I.Sam.28. Videndus quo-que Augustinus lib. 2. ad Simplicianum, quaest. 3 ubi hanc quaestionem in dubio reliquit, nec quicquam certi definit. Credibilius tamen daemonem in forma Samuelis apparuisse, quem opinabatur Samuelem esse: ex quo discere cupiebat eventum belli, quod tum cum Allophylis gerebat. Quo facit tamen hic theolo-gicus, Species rerum appellantur de nominibus ipsa-rum rerum.
units.tr: Samuel] a demon in the appearance of Samuel, whom Scripture calls Samuel in the manner of speaking by which it calls angels men or men-of-God, and as Raphael in the history of Tobit is called Azarias son of Ananias; or Samuel himself, whom God permitted to be raised so that he might foretell the future to his then king. Those who defend this opinion split into two views. Some think his soul was raised; others, only his body. This kind of magic is called necromancy, when, namely, we divine through the dead and foretell what is to come. On this matter, besides Nicolaus, consult Paul, bishop of Burgos, in his Additions on 1 Sam. 28. See also Augustine, book 2 to Simplicianus, question 3, where he leaves this question in doubt and defines nothing certain. It is more credible, however, that a demon appeared in the form of Samuel, whom she supposed to be Samuel, and from whom she wished to learn the outcome of the war which he was then waging against the Allophyles. Yet this theologian's point here fits: the species of things are so called from the names of the things themselves.

units.la: Cum filio] cum filiis potius. Paullo post, filij regis cadunt. Nam tres erant numero; Ionathan, Abinadab & Melchisna[?].
units.tr: With the son] rather, with the sons. A little after, the king's sons fall. For there were three in number: Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua.

units.la: Saul equo delapsus
units.tr: Saul thrown from his horse

units.la: In actibus Apostolorum XL. annos regnasse dictus est
units.tr: In the Acts of the Apostles he is said to have reigned forty years

units.la: Triginta eum annos regnasse annotaverunt
units.tr: They have noted that he reigned thirty years

units.la: Etiam Samuelis annos sub regis iitius aetate numeratos
units.tr: Also Samuel's years counted under the king's age

units.la: Pag. 61, Arca in Cariath-jarim opidum translata
units.tr: Page 61. The ark transferred to the town of Kiriath-jearim

units.la: Cum per XX. annos ibi constitisset
units.tr: After it had stayed there for twenty years

units.la: Cum Eli sacerdote natus] Salmanticensis, Samuel agebat annum 19. cum diem suum obiret Eli. Nam Eli coepit judicare quum Hanna mater Samuelis precatum venisset. Hæc ille.
units.tr: Born in the time of Eli the priest] The Salmanticensis: Samuel was in his nineteenth year when Eli was about to die. For Eli began to judge when Hannah, Samuel's mother, had come praying. So he.

units.la: Admodum senex sacerdotio functus] locus iste suspectum facit Sulpicium erroris, & omnino erravit, si putavit Samuelem summum sacerdotem fuisse. Quomodo enim pontifex esse potuit, qui ne sacerdos quidem erat? Dico sacerdos, ut nomen hoc vulgo sumitur. Alioqui levites erat, ut & judex & prophetes. Quod supra mihi observatum.
units.tr: Having served as priest when very old] This passage makes Sulpicius suspect of error, and he was wrong altogether if he thought Samuel was high priest. For how could he be high priest when he was not even a priest? I say "priest" as the word is commonly taken. Otherwise he was a Levite, as well as judge and prophet. This I noted above.

units.la: LXX. annis præfuisse populo refertur] quærendum quinam chronologi sic sentiant, & an non potius legendum sit XX annis: quæ autoritas a Josepho assumpta.
units.tr: He is reported to have ruled the people for seventy years] We must ask which chronologers think so, and whether it should not rather be read as twenty years; this is the authority taken from Josephus.

units.la: Chronicorum.] Eusebij Verba sunt: Ebræorum primus rex Saul ex tribu Benjamin & Samuel ann.40.
units.tr: Of the Chronicles.] These are the words of Eusebius: the first king of the Hebrews was Saul of the tribe of Benjamin, and Samuel for forty years.

units.la: Flevisse traditur] non tam de Davide hoc dicitur, quam de iis qui cum eo erant, 2.Reg 1.11.
units.tr: He is said to have wept] This is said not so much of David as of those who were with him, 2 Sam. 1. 11.

units.la: Chebron] vel Hebron. Sic Chermon & Hermon. Hoc opidum septem annis ante Tanim Ægypti conditum perhibetur.
units.tr: Hebron] or Hebron. So Chermon and Hermon. This town is said to have been founded seven years before Tanis in Egypt.

units.la: Iudæ[?] opidum] ut supra, in terram Iudæ regressus, ubi vulgati codices, in terram Iudæ. Vide quæ notavimus ad hunc locum. Sic Bethlehem Iudæ & Iudææ, variantibus libris. Erat & tractus montosus, qui Hebron sive Chebron dicebatur: unde 2.Sam 2.3, habitarunt in opidis Hebron. Nisi opida ibi posuit pro opido, ut montes Gelboe, flumina Nili, & quæ alia Grammatici annotarunt. Forsan opida Hebron appellat vicinos ejus. Cui firmando quod 1.Machab. 5.65. τὸ[?] Χεβρὼν καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας αὐτῆς.
units.tr: The town of Judah] as above, he returned into the land of Judah, where the common codices read "into the land of Judah." See what we noted on this passage. So Bethlehem of Judah and of Judaea, the books varying. There was also a mountainous district which was called Hebron or Chebron, whence 2 Sam. 2. 3: they dwelt in the towns of Hebron. Unless he calls the towns there by the name of the town, as the mountains of Gilboa, the rivers of the Nile, and other things the grammarians have noted. Perhaps he calls the towns near it "Hebron." To confirm this, 1 Macc. 5. 65: [Chebron] and its daughters.

units.la: Rex appellatus est] a tribu Iuda tantum. Salmanticensis, David coepit regnare anno creationis 2884[?]. Post trigesi-mum septimum annum regni ejus rebellavit Absalom, quemadmodum dicitur, & fuit a fine 40. annorum. Hi anni numerantur ab eo tempore quo postularunt sibi regem. Et aliquanto post, David regnavit 40. annis.
units.tr: He was called king] by the tribe of Judah only. Salmanticensis: David began to reign in the year of creation 2884. In the thirty-seventh year of his reign Absalom rebelled, as is said, and he reigned from the end of forty years. These years are counted from the time they asked for a king for themselves. And a little after: David reigned forty years.

units.la: Pag.62. Ilbaal] Sic vocatur, 1.Paralip. 8.33 ubi Lat. vetus, Esbaal. Ceterum 2.Sam.2.8. Isbofeth nominatur.
units.tr: Page 62. Ishbaal] So he is called in 1 Chron. 8. 33, where the old Latin has Esbaal. But in 2 Sam. 2. 8 he is named Ishbosheth.

units.la: Fratrem Ioab] nomine Asael.
units.tr: The brother of Joab] by the name Asahel.

units.la: Quo dolore postea Ioab] vera causa erat, ut Josephus refert, quod miserè timeret ne honore, quem obtinebat, privare-tur. Datur, Davide imperium exercitus in Abnerem transferente. Orig. Iud. lib. 7. cap. 1.
units.tr: With what grief Joab afterwards] the true cause, as Josephus reports, was that he feared wretchedly that he would be deprived of the honour he held, when the command of the army was given to Abner by David. Antiquities of the Jews, book 7, chapter 1.

units.la: Iugulari eum praecepit] imo ipse jugulavit eum. 2. Samuel 3.27.
units.tr: He ordered him to be slain] nay, he himself slew him, 2 Sam. 3. 27.

units.la: Omnes fere natu majores] cur adjecit fere? nam nemo excipitur. Ceterum universæ tribus ei regni detulerunt, cum prius seniores cum eo fœdus pepigissent. Quidam scribunt primum universas tribus, deinde omnes seniores venisse in Hebron, ibique eum unxisse regem super Israel. Vide 1. Sam. 5.1. & 3.
units.tr: Almost all the elders by birth] Why did he add "almost"? For no one is excepted. Moreover all the tribes offered him the kingdom, after the elders had first made a covenant with him. Some write that first all the tribes, then all the elders came to Hebron, and there anointed him king over Israel. See 1 Sam. 5. 1 and 3.

units.la: Per septem annos] & sex menses, 2. Sam. 5.5.
units.tr: For seven years] and six months, 2 Sam. 5. 5.

units.la: In Sion translulit] prius in domum Obed-edom, ubi fuit per tres menses. Sion autem alio nomine urbs David appellatur & superior civitas.
units.tr: He moved it into Zion] first into the house of Obed-edom, where it stayed for three months. Zion is also called by another name the city of David and the upper city.

units.la: Semini illius] filio Salomoni. Nota semen de uno dici. Sic Gen. 4.25. posuit mihi semen pro Habel. Sensus est, dedit mihi filium alium.
units.tr: To his seed] to his son Solomon. Note that "seed" is said of one. So Gen. 4. 25: God has appointed me seed in place of Abel. The sense is: he gave me another son.

units.la: Syriam] Damascenam.
units.tr: Syria] of Damascus.

units.la: Stipendiumque ei impo-suit] id est, tributum, ut pag. 68. cum laxari sibi stipendium popos-cisset, quod Salomon gravissimum impo-suerat. Sic alibi passim in hoc libro, ut 78. 85. 98. 119. 130. & 132.
units.tr: And imposed tribute on him] that is, a tax, as on page 68, when they had asked that the tribute imposed by Solomon, which was very heavy, be relaxed. So elsewhere throughout this book, as at 78, 85, 98, 119, 130 and 132.

units.la: Ex praeda] quam de Adar et Ezer rege Soba sive Sophenorum ceperat, 2. Sam. 8.7. ex hoc are post omnia vasa templi aenea confecta fuerunt, 2. Sam. 8.8.
units.tr: From the spoil] which he had taken from Hadadezer king of Zobah or of the Sophenes, 2 Sam. 8. 7. From this bronze, after all the vessels of the temple, the bronze vessels were made, 2 Sam. 8. 8.

units.la: Ammonitas] filios Ammon.
units.tr: The Ammonites] the sons of Ammon.

units.la: Chanun regis eorum] vel, Chanon sive Hanon, quod scribunt Anon, sine aspiratione. In editione Graeca est Ann-um duplici N. 2. Sam. 10.1. Chanon, Hanon, ut Cham, Ham. Chebron, Hebron; Chermon, Hermon.
units.tr: Hanun, their king] or Chanon or Hanon, which some write Anon, without the aspiration. In the Greek edition it is written with a double N. 2 Sam. 10. 1: Chanon, Hanon, as Cham, Ham; Chebron, Hebron; Chermon, Hermon.

units.la: Syris denuo rebellantibus] nam Ammonitae mercede conduxerant eos ad hoc bellum.
units.tr: The Syrians rebelling again] for the Ammonites had hired them for pay for this war.

units.la: Berfaben quandam] secutus errorem Graecorum vocat Ber-faben, quae in Ebraeis & Latinis codicibus Bethsabe dicitur: quem errorem libenter scribis imputaverim quam interpretibus. Videtur natus ex affinitate litterarum 9 & ρ.
units.tr: Following the Greek error, he calls her Ber-faben, which in the Hebrew and Latin codices is called Bethsabe. One may more willingly impute this error to scribes than to translators. It seems to have arisen from the similarity of the letters 9 and ρ.

units.la: Viri cujusdam] Uriae Hetthaei.
units.tr: Of Uriah the Hittite.

units.la: In castris erat] ante Rabbath filiorum Ammon.
units.tr: Before Rabbath of the sons of Ammon.

units.la: Multaque in domum, &c] Thamar vi compressa. Ammon, qui eam compresserat, occisus a fratre Abfalomo. Quae duo sunt execranda crimina, videlicet incestus & fraternum parricidium.
units.tr: Tamar was violated by force. Amnon, who had violated her, was killed by his brother Absalom. These are two detestable crimes, namely incest and fratricide.

units.la: Absalon] mendum quale in Abiron. Veritas scriptura Absalom, cum M in fine. Contra peccatum in μαδιὰμ, quod Ebræi scribunt Madian, cum N in fine.
units.tr: An error of the same kind as in Abiron. The true Scripture form is Absalom, with M at the end. Compare the error in Madian [Μαδιάμ], which the Hebrews write Madian, with N at the end.

units.la: Arma ipia] vere impia. Nam pietas contra parentem arma ferre prohibet.
units.tr: Truly impious arms. For piety forbids bearing arms against a parent.

units.la: Parricidae filio] parricidam appellat quia patrem occidere conabatur, aut quia fratrem occiderat. Quamvis & pro eo usurpetur qui nefas aliquod impium in patria perniciem fuerit machinatus.
units.tr: He calls him a parricide because he tried to kill his father, or because he had killed his brother. Yet the word is also used of one who has plotted some impious crime to the ruin of his country.

units.la: Aliud rursum exortum] Sigonius legendum opinatur, cum aliud rursum exortum: quod non improbo.
units.tr: Sigonius thinks it should be read "cum aliud rursum exortum" (when something else arose again). I do not disapprove.

units.la: Sabæa] malim, Sabea, qui & Sabee in edit. Rom. id est, Cus. Editio Lat. vulgata, Seba filius Bochri, vir Iemineus, id est, Benjamita. In Ebraeo [illegible, ~3 letters] quod antiquitus Sabe legebatur, ut [illegible, ~3 letters] Phare: unde Photiphares.
units.tr: I would prefer Sabea, which is also Sabee in the Roman edition, that is, Cush. The published Latin Vulgate has Seba son of Bochri, a man of Jemini, that is, a Benjamite. In the Hebrew, which was anciently read Sabe, as ... Phare, whence Photiphares.

units.la: Praelia fecundo eventu habuit] Sic pag. 41. fecundo eventu praelium fecit: ubi tamen alij codices, fecundum eventu praelium fecit. Vide quae notavimus ad illum locum.
units.tr: So on p. 41 he "fought a battle with a fortunate outcome" (fecundo eventu praelium fecit), though other copies there read "fecundum eventu praelium fecit". See what we noted on that passage.

units.la: Decies centena, &c.] Israelitarum octingenta millia & Iu-dæorum quingenta.
units.tr: Eight hundred thousand Israelites and five hundred thousand of Judah.

units.la: Cur in id] quod in id. Sigonius, probo vehementer.
units.tr: Read "quod in id" rather than "cur in id". Sigonius; I strongly approve.

units.la: Angelus] propheta Gad. Notum illud, quoniam angelus Domini exercituum est. Similiter sacerdotes angeli vocantur.
units.tr: The prophet Gad. It is well known that "the angel of the Lord of hosts" is meant. Likewise priests are called angels.

units.la: Triennij fame] τρία ἔτη λιμὸς ἐν τῇ γῇ σου ἐστὶν ἐν Γραικῇ editione, 2.Reg.24.13. ut etiam in codicibus Ebræis, 1.Paralip. 21.12. qui tamen in priore loco habent septem annis. Quod sequendo legendum esset, septennii fame.
units.tr: The Greek edition at 2 Sam. 24:13 has "three years of famine in your land" [τρία ἔτη λιμὸς ἐν τῇ γῇ σου], as also do the Hebrew codices at 1 Chron. 21:12, though in the former passage they have seven years. Following that, one would have to read "a famine of seven years".

units.la: Trium mensium fuga] aut tribus mensibus fugies ad-versarios tuos, & illi te persequenter, 2.Sam.24.13. in Latina vulgata.
units.tr: "Or flee three months before your adversaries, while they pursue you," 2 Sam. 24:13 in the Latin Vulgate.

units.la: Morte triduij] aut certe tribus diebus erit pestilentia in terra tua, ibidem.
units.tr: "Or certainly there will be pestilence in your land for three days," ibid.

units.la: Mortem elegit] i. pestilentiam, quam & Chaldaei [illegible, ~4 letters] vocant: etiam interpres vetus, Psal. 91.3. a morte insidiarum, ubi codex Ebraeus, a lue, sive a pestilentia. Gallice mortalité.
units.tr: That is, pestilence, which the Chaldeans also call by this name. So too the old translator at Ps. 91:3, "from the death of snares," where the Hebrew codex has "from the plague, or from pestilence." In French, mortalité.

units.la: Momentoque] non momento, sed a mane usque ad tempus constitutum, quod Moed vocant Ebraei. Id alij de vespera, alij de meridie accipiunt. LXX. habent ἕως ὥρας ἑσπέρας[?] usque ad horam horam prandij.
units.tr: Not "in a moment," but from morning until the appointed time, which the Hebrews call Moed. Others take it of evening, others of midday. The LXX have "until the hour of evening" [ἕως ὥρας ἑσπέρας], that is, until the hour of dinner.

units.la: Seque vivum pro omnibus] vide num legendum sit, seque unum pro omnibus?
units.tr: See whether it should be read "and himself alone for all."

units.la: Pag.65. In loco, in quo angelum viderat] in area Areunae (alias Ornae) Iebusaei.
units.tr: P. 65. In the place where he had seen the angel: in the threshing floor of Araunah (otherwise Ornan) the Jebusite.

units.la: Salomonem filium] Salmanticensis, David obiit anno mundi 3924. & tunc incoepit regnare Salomo filius ejus, qui anno quarto regni sui coepit ædificare templum, videlicet an. mundi 3928. in quo completi sunt anni 480. exitus ex Ægypto. Nam anno 448. egressi sunt.
units.tr: The Salamanca Jew: David died in the year of the world 3924, and then Solomon his son began to reign. In the fourth year of his reign he began to build the temple, namely in the year of the world 3928, in which the 480 years from the exodus from Egypt were completed. For they went out in 448.

units.la: Uriae uxore] quae fuerat Uria uxor.
units.tr: Who had been the wife of Uriah.

units.la: Incolumi] vivente.
units.tr: Living.

units.la: Rex appellatus] desideratur verbum substantivum, ut pag. 74. sed misi coelesti igne absumpti. Hic sunt, ibi est jubau-diendum. Aut legendum, rex appellatur. Potest etiam locus hoc modo distingui, rex appellatus: David, cum regnasset annos XL. defunctus est, ut verbum est ad utrumque membrum pertineat.
units.tr: The substantive verb is lacking here, as on p. 74, "but were consumed by heavenly fire." Here "they are," there "is" must be supplied. Or read "rex appellatur." The passage may also be punctuated thus: "rex appellatus: David, when he had reigned forty years, died," so that the verb belongs to both clauses.

units.la: Annos XL.] regnavit in Hebron, septem annos & sex menses, in Ierusalem vero triginta tres. Simul efficiunt annos 40. omisso minore numero.
units.tr: He reigned in Hebron seven years and six months, but in Jerusalem thirty-three. Together these make forty years, the smaller number being omitted.

units.la: Regali unguento unctus] hoc fiebat propter Adoniam regni competitorem. Alioqui filij regum non ungebantur. Vide 100[?] sol.191. col.4. & sol.211. col.1.
units.tr: This was done on account of Adonijah, the rival for the kingdom. Otherwise the sons of kings were not anointed. See p. 100 and p. 191, col. 4, and p. 211, col. 1.

units.la: Urbem] Ierosolymam, 1.Reg 3.1.
units.tr: Jerusalem, 1 Kings 3:1.

units.la: Ante sacrarium] ante arcam foederis.
units.tr: Before the ark of the covenant.

units.la: Cum eodem tempore pueros edidissent] intervallum erat dierum trium. Quando autem mortuus fuerit alter puer Scriptura non prodidit. Vide 1.Reg.3.18.
units.tr: There was an interval of three days. When the other boy died, Scripture does not tell. See 1 Kings 3:18.

units.la: De puero] vivente.
units.tr: Living.

units.la: Tum Salomon] cum hujusmodi nomina Latine in O finiantur, ut Zeno, Plato, Iafo: nullum etiam sit N in nomine Ebraico, quis neget scribendum esse Salomo potius quam Salomon? tamen ut recepta consuetudine aliter obtineat.
units.tr: Since names of this kind end in O in Latin, such as Zeno, Plato, Iafo, and since the Hebrew name has no N in it, who would deny that it ought to be written Salomo rather than Salomon? Yet by accepted custom the other form prevails.

units.la: Anno fere octavo & octogesimo & quingentesimo] Apud Iosephum Rufini, anno quingentesimo secundo. Sed in exemplari Graeco, [illegible, ~20 letters] quingentesimo nonagesimo secundo.
units.tr: In Josephus, in the Rufinus version, the year is the 502nd. But in the Greek copy it is the 592nd.

units.la: CCCC.XL.] 3.Reg.6. [illegible, ~25 letters]
units.tr: 440. 3 Kings 6.

units.la: [?]σιοσῷ ἔτει τῆς ἐξόδου ἡμῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου. Sic editio Roma-na. In Complutensi est ἐν τῷ ὀγδοηκοστῷ, id est, octogesimo. Sic veritas Ebraica. Autor Seder Olam non dissentit. Salmanticen-sis Iudæus, Anno quarto regni sui coepit Salomo extruere templum, ann. mundi 3918[?]. quo tempore finiunt ann. 480, egressionis ex Ægypto. Nam anno 448. egressi sunt.
units.tr: "In the eightieth year of our going out of Israel from Egypt" [ὀγδοηκοστῷ ἔτει τῆς ἐξόδου ἡμῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου]. So the Roman edition. The Complutensian has "in the eightieth" [ἐν τῷ ὀγδοηκοστῷ], that is, the eightieth, as the Hebrew truth has it. The author of Seder Olam does not dissent. The Salamanca Jew: in the fourth year of his reign Solomon began to build the temple, in the year of the world 3918, at which time the 480 years from the going out from Egypt end. For they went out in 448.

units.la: Quod nequaquam convenit] imo convenit optime. Nam anno altero Iephthae habitaverât Israelitæ in opido Hesebon ann. 300. Ab eo anno usque ad quartum Salomonis numerantur anni 140. His adde 40. quibus vagati sunt per desertum, habes annos 480.
units.tr: Indeed it agrees very well. For in the second year of Jephthah the Israelites had dwelt in the town of Heshbon for 300 years. From that year to the fourth year of Solomon are counted 140 years. Add to these the 40 years in which they wandered in the desert, and you have 480 years.

units.la: Quam ut propheta erraverit] Si prophetes errare non potest, possunt librarij, etiam in libris sacris. Quod miror quosdam tam pertinanter negare. Nam in narratione Stephani Act. 7. quin aliquoties erraverint, ne Carneades quidem negaverit.
units.tr: If a prophet cannot err, scribes can, even in sacred books. I wonder that some deny this so stubbornly. For in Stephen's speech in Acts 7, that they have erred several times not even Carneades would deny.

units.la: Explicuit] absolvit, ut infra 107. nihil territus coepta explicuit. Sic explicare iter pro perficere: &, rem tibi explicatam reddo, id est, perfectam.
units.tr: Finished, as below, p. 107: "undismayed, he completed what he had begun." So "explicare iter" is used for "perficere," and "rem tibi explicatam reddo" means "I return the matter to you finished," that is, perfected.

units.la: Ex alienigenis conjugia sumpsisset] id est, uxores alienigenas, videlicet filiam Pharaonis regis Ægypti, Moabitidas, Ammonitidas, Idumæas, Sidonias, Chetthæas, 3. Reg. 11.1. Vt hic, conjugia ex alienigenis sumere: ita supra 40. dixit matrimonia ex victis assumere.
units.tr: That is, foreign wives: namely the daughter of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite women, 1 Kings 11:1. As here "to take marriages from foreigners," so above, p. 40, he said "to take matrimonies from the conquered."

units.la: Idola] simulachra Chamosi, Astartes & Molochi.
units.tr: Images of Chemosh, Ashtoreth and Molech.

units.la: Servo illius] Ieroboamo.
units.tr: Jeroboam.

units.la: Sexto & decimo] corrige audacter uno & quadragesimo, ex 2. Paralip. 12. 13. Error, ut apparet, ex numeris. Nam proclivis profecto lapsus de xlj. in xvj.
units.tr: Boldly correct "sixteenth" to "forty-first," from 2 Chron. 12:13. The error is evidently one of numerals, for a slip from forty-one to sixteen is very easy.

units.la: Regnum patrium] præferrem, paternum: nisi Sulpicio patrius & paternus promiscue usurpari scirem. Sane urbem paternam idem dixit pro patriam, infra 106.
units.tr: I would prefer "paternum," unless I knew that Sulpicius used patrius and paternus interchangeably. Indeed he also said "urbem paternam" for "patriam," below, p. 106.

units.la: Pag.68. Pars populi] decem tribus.
units.tr: P. 68. Part of the people: the ten tribes.

units.la: Hieroboam] codex Parisiensis, Ieroboam: in aliis est Hieroboam: quomodo Sulpicium scripsisse putarim. ei simile Hierusalem pro Ierusalem. Ceterum duo fuerunt hoc nomine. Ieroboam senior, qui patrem habuit Nabat dictum, & junior, qui filius Ioas vocatur, Amos. 1.1.
units.tr: The Paris codex has "Ieroboam"; in others it is "Hieroboam," as I suspect Sulpicius wrote, just as "Hierusalem" for "Ierusalem." There were two men of this name: Jeroboam the elder, whose father was called Nabat, and the younger, who is called the son of Joash, Amos 1:1.

units.la: Medio genere ortus] neque regio, neque plebeio, sed medio inter utrumque. Pater ei Nabat, ut diximus, mater Serua. Genere autem
units.tr: Neither royal nor plebeian, but of middle rank between the two. His father was Nabat, as we said, and his mother Serua. By birth...

units.la: In AEgyptum confugit] ad Sefac regem AEgypti.
units.tr: To Shishak, king of Egypt.

units.la: Ibique uxore accepta ex stirpe regia] hoc de Hadad Idumæo Scriptura prodidit. Vide 3 Reg. 11. 19.
units.tr: Scripture records this of Hadad the Edomite. See 1 Kings 11:19.

units.la: Duæ tribus] una habebatur 3 Reg. 11. 36. sed sub hac una comprehendebatur etiam tribus Benjamin. Vide quoq; 3 Reg. 12. 20.
units.tr: One tribe is counted at 1 Kings 11:36, but under this one was included also the tribe of Benjamin. See also 1 Kings 12:20.

units.la: Ad trecenta millia] legendum, ad ducenta millia. Nam erant centum octoginta millia. Quam vis in editione Romana [?] 3 Reg. 12. 21.
units.tr: Read "two hundred thousand," for there were 180,000. Although in the Roman edition ... 1 Kings 12:21.

units.la: Verbis Dei] per Semeiam virum Dei, i. prophetam.
units.tr: Through Shemaiah, the man of God, that is, the prophet.

units.la: Ne ab eo] malum, ne a se.
units.tr: Read "ne a se" (lest from himself) rather than "ne ab eo" (lest from him).

units.la: Pag. 69. Vaccam auream] quam hic vaccam dicit, alij vitulum, alij bovem vocant. Vacca etiam dicitur, Tob. 1. 5. [?] id est, vaccæ Lex. Græco Lat. vetus, bucula, juvenca, vacca. Sed & vocem [?] quam nunc vitulas reddunt, interpres vetus vaccas exposuit, Hof. 10. 5. In LXX. quoque [?] ibid. verf. 11. Vituli vox usitatior est. Sed Hof. 13. 2. [?] vitulos, Ionathan convertit boves. [?] est bos, quis culpet Sulpicium [?] vaccam reddentis Contra Psal. 1 c. 5 21 & Num. 7. 3 bos a LXX. redditur [?] Videndus hac de re Augustinus, cujus verba invenies alibi in his notis.
units.tr: Page 69. The golden heifer: which he here calls a heifer, others a calf, and others an ox. It is also called a heifer at Tob. 1.5 [?], that is, "of the heifers." The old Greek-Latin lexicon gives heifer, young cow, and cow for the word. The old translator rendered the calves that they now give back as heifers, Hos. 10.5. The Seventy also use, at the same passage, verse 11, the more common word for calf. But at Hos. 13.2 Jonathan translates the calves as oxen. It is an ox; who would blame Sulpicius for rendering it heifer? Against Ps. 1 c. 5 21, and at Num. 7.3, the LXX render ox. On this matter Augustine should be consulted; you will find his words elsewhere in these notes.

units.la: Ex plebe] ex plebe infima, pro quo 3 Reg. 12. 31. de extremis populi, & in LXX. [?] partem aliquam e populo.
units.tr: Of the common people: of the lowest of the people. At 3 Kings 12.31 the same phrase means from the extremes of the people, and in the LXX, some part of the people.

units.la: Expostulatio consecuta] per prophetam quendam Iadon nomine. Sic Iosephus eum appellat, Orig lib. 8. cap 3.
units.tr: A rebuke followed: through a certain prophet named Iadon. So Josephus calls him, Origen book 8, chapter 3.

units.la: Abiud] mendum quale pag. 31 ubi Abiud pro Abihu legitur. Sic hoc loco legendum Abiu, abjecta D, nempe ex Græco [?] quod in editione Romana 3 Reg. 15. 1. pro quo in fonte Abiam. Sed 2 Paralip. 12. 16. Abia legitur & Græce [?] Par varietas in [?] & [?].
units.tr: Abiud: an error like that on page 31, where Abiud is read for Abihu. So here we should read Abiu, with the D dropped, from the Greek, which in the Roman edition at 3 Kings 15.1 is given for the original Abiam. But at 2 Chron. 12.16 Abia is read, and in Greek also. There is variation in the [?].

units.la: Sex annos tenuit: quāvis in Chronicis triennio regnasse referatur] ad historiæ fidem emendat Sigonius, tres annos tenuit: quamvis in Chronicis sex annis regnasse referatur.
units.tr: He reigned six years, although in the Chronicles it is said that he reigned for three years: Sigonius emends to the historical account: he reigned three years, although in the Chronicles it is said that he reigned six years.

units.la: Mirari fatis non possum. Nam in Chronicis Eusebij, post quem Abiam annis tribus, nisi legendum hoc loco, annis sex. Sane scriptum lectum, 2 Paralip. 13.1. tribus annis regnavit, & in LXX. Ἰφια ἔτη ἐβασίλευσεν [?]. Idem numerus, 3 Reg. 15.2.
units.tr: I cannot marvel enough at the facts. For in the Chronicles of Eusebius, after whom Abiam [reigned] three years, unless it is to be read here as six years. Certainly the text reads at 2 Chron. 13.1, "he reigned three years," and in the LXX, "three years he reigned" [Greek]. The same number is at 3 Kings 15.2.

units.la: Asab] rectum est Asa. Nam etiam in LXX. legitur ἀσά [?]. 3 Reg. 15.
units.tr: Asab: the correct form is Asa. For it is also read in the LXX as Asa [Greek], 3 Kings 15.

units.la: Quintus [?] fere] quartus erat a Davide, ut ex serie regum videre licet, Salomo, Roboam, Abiam, Asa. Sane Davidis filius Salomo erat, nepos Roboam, pronepos Abiam, abnepos vero, ideo filius pronepotis, Asa. Ideo sequitur, quippe abnepos ejus.
units.tr: The fifth, nearly: he was the fourth from David, as can be seen from the series of kings: Solomon, Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa. Certainly Solomon was David's son, Rehoboam his grandson, Abijah his great-grandson, and Asa his great-great-grandson, and therefore a son of a great-grandson. Hence it follows, since he was his great-great-grandson.

units.la: Quod autem in Chronicis Eusebij, post quem quintus Asa, an. 41. Id aliter legitur in editis a Scaligero, Hebræorum Juda rex quintus Asa, ann. 41.
units.tr: But what is in Eusebius's Chronicle, after whom the fifth, Asa, in the 41st year. This is read differently in the editions of Scaliger: the fifth king of the Hebrew Judah, Asa, in the 41st year.

units.la: Cum rege Syriæ] Benhadado.
units.tr: With the king of Syria: Benhadad.

units.la: Auxilio Ieroboæ] Sic declinant Adam, Adæ; Abraham, Abrahæ. Nam est obliquus a recto Ieroboam.
units.tr: By the help of Jeroboam: they decline Adam, Adae; Abraham, Abrahae, in this way. For the oblique case is from the nominative Jeroboam.

units.la: A filio tenebatur] non a filio, sed a Baasa, qui filium ejus occiderat, eique in regno successerat. Vide sequentia.
units.tr: He was held by his son: not by his son, but by Baasha, who had killed his son and succeeded him in the kingdom. See what follows.

units.la: Quod societate regis Syriæ nimium confisus fit] 2 Paralip. 16,7. Qui habuit fiduciam in rege Syriæ, &c.
units.tr: Because he trusted too much in the alliance of the king of Syria: 2 Chron. 16.7, "who had confidence in the king of Syria," etc.

units.la: In vinculo conjecit] ibid. vers. 10.
units.tr: He cast him into prison: ibid. verse 10.

units.la: In pedum dolore, &c.] v. 12. Aegrotavit etiam Asa an. 39. regni sui dolore pedum vehementissimo, nec in infirmitate sua quæsivit Dominum, sed magis in medicorum arte confisus est. Verba sunt interpretis vulgati, loco superius citato.
units.tr: In the pain of his feet, etc.: verse 12.
