units.tr: Valens from Mursia] which is also Mursa, a city of Lower Pannonia, where Vetranio was formerly made emperor and Magnentius was defeated. Below it is called Morsa. Jerome, against the Luciferians: Valens, bishop of Mursa.

units.la: Ab Heraclia Theodorus] hic est Theodorus episcopus Heraclea, Athanasio memoratus. Ceterum Heraclea magis ustitatum. Sic Arius et Arem: Darius et Dareus: Augiæ et Augeæ stabulum.
units.tr: Theodorus from Heraclia] This is Theodorus, bishop of Heraclea, mentioned by Athanasius. Heraclea, however, is the more usual form, as with Arius and Areus, Darius and Dareus, and the stable of Augeas and Augias.

units.la: Stephanus Antiochenus] qui Placillo successit etiam Arriano. Nam Antiochia post Eustachium vigesimum tertium episcopum, quem Ariani egerunt in exilium, continuos habuit episcopos Arrianos undecim; quos Hiero. ait hostes Christi, non episcopos, fuisse. Vide Chronicon Eusebij.
units.tr: Stephanus of Antioch] who succeeded Placillus, also an Arian. For Antioch, after Eustathius, its twenty-third bishop, whom the Arians drove into exile, had eleven successive Arian bishops, whom Jerome says were enemies of Christ, not bishops. See Eusebius's Chronicle.

units.la: Pag. 149. Acatius] vel Acacius, ut Ursatius & Ursacius.
units.tr: Page 149. Acatius] or Acacius, as Ursatius and Ursacius.

units.la: Menophanes] alii Menophantes sive Menophantus dicitur. In Athanasio, Menophantus Ephesi episcopus.
units.tr: Menophanes] Others call him Menophantes or Menophantus. In Athanasius, Menophantus is bishop of Ephesus.

units.la: Ephesio] cur non dixit, ab Ephesio, ut a Cæsarea, ab Heraclea? Ad quod exemplum dicere debuit, a Laodicea.
units.tr: From Ephesus] Why did he not say "from Ephesus", as "from Caesarea" and "from Heraclea"? By that pattern he should have said "from Laodicea".

units.la: Georgius] Laodiceæ episcopus Cappadox, Arrianorum ζόταλ[?], Athanasius. In eodem, Acacius Cæsareæ Palæstinæ episcopus Arrianus, Eusebij Pamphili discipulus.
units.tr: Georgius] bishop of Laodicea, a Cappadocian, of the Arian party, according to Athanasius. In the same work, Acacius, Arian bishop of Caesarea in Palestine, a disciple of Eusebius Pamphili.

units.la: Narcissus a Neapoli] leg. a Neropoli, vel certe, ut Sigonius annotavit, a Neronipoli. In Athanasij, Narcissus episcopus Neropoleos vel Neroniadis, caput Arrianorum.
units.tr: Narcissus from Naples] Read "from Neropolis", or certainly, as Sigonius noted, "from Neronipolis". In Athanasius, Narcissus is bishop of Neropolis or Neroniadis, the head of the Arians.

units.la: Apud Morsam] Hieron. in Chronico, Magnentius Mursæ victus, in quo prælio Romanæ vires conciderunt.
units.tr: At Mursa] Jerome, in the Chronicle: Magnentius was defeated at Mursa, in which battle the Roman forces were broken.

units.la: Eusebius Vercellensium] sic mox ait, Hilarius Pictavorum episcopus. Hic a Hieronymo & aliis dicitur, Vercellensis episcopus. Meminit Hiero. epist. LXXV. quæ adversus Vigilantium, Vercellensis Eusebius omnium Psalmorum commentarios hæretici hominis (Origenem intelligit) vertit in nostrum eloquium: licet hæretica prætermittens optima quæque transtulerit.
units.tr: Eusebius of Vercelli] Thus he says soon after, Hilary, bishop of Poitiers. This man is called by Jerome and others bishop of Vercelli. Jerome mentions him in letter 75, which is against Vigilantius: Eusebius of Vercelli translated into our language all the commentaries on the Psalms of that heretical man (he means Origen), omitting the heretical matter and rendering all that was best.

units.la: Lucifer a Caranalis] Vitior emendat a Caralis: Galsfinim[?] vero, Caralensis. Lucifer a Caralis ita dicitur, ut supra Vr- satus a Singiduno: Valensa Murfia: Theodorus ab Hera- clea. In Paufania χαρναλις, unde forte Caranalis. Aut legen- dum χαρναλις Sane alibi est de Sardinia Caraval episcopus. Reperio et Caralitanus episcopus. Ab hoc Luciferiani nucupati, Mediolanensium sacerdos] imo episcopus. ita vocatur A- thanafio & Hieronymo. Verba Hieronymi, Lucifer ac Diony- fius Caralitanae & Mediolanensis ecclesiae episcopi.
units.tr: Lucifer from Caranalis] Vitus emends it to "from Caralis", and Galsfinius (?) to "Caralensis". Lucifer is so called "from Caralis", just as above Ursatius is "from Singidunum", Valens "from Mursa", and Theodorus "from Heraclea". In Pausanias [χαρναλις], whence perhaps Caranalis; or one should read [χαρναλις]. Indeed elsewhere there is mention of Caraval, bishop of Sardinia, and I also find a Caralitan bishop. From him the Luciferians were named. Bishop of Milan] nay, bishop; so he is called by Athanasius and Jerome. The words of Jerome: "Lucifer and Dionysius, bishops of the Caralitan and Milanese churches."

units.la: Relegati] in partibus vicinis Aegypto, Pag. 151. Non ausi piacula profiteri] piacula vocat haere- sin Arrianam, ut pag. 152. palam ac publice haeresis piacu- la praedicabant. & mox, eoque his certaminibus procef- sum, ut iftiuimodi piaculis orbis terrarum implicaretur.
units.tr: "Relegati": banished to parts near Egypt, p. 151. "Not daring to profess the abominations": he calls the Arian heresy "abominations," as on p. 152, where they publicly proclaimed the heresy's abominations. And soon after: the conflicts went so far that the whole world was entangled in such abominations.

units.la: Dionysius] de quo supra, qui Mediolanensium episcopus e- rat, non Albae metropolis Italorum, ut existimat Gifelinus. Ad- hibenotas ejus ad hunc locum.
units.tr: Dionysius: the one mentioned above, who was bishop of the Milanese, not of Alba, the metropolis of the Italians, as Gifelinus thinks. Compare his notes at this place.

units.la: In ejus locum episcopus subrogatur] Athanafius tom.a. Auxentius Cappadox Dionysio successit. Reste igitur Sigo- nius, ejus in locum Auxentius episcopus subrogatur. Nam ipsa res clamat aliquid abesse. Auxentij mentio & apud Hiero. epift. LVII. quae ad Damasum,
units.tr: "In his place a bishop is appointed": Athanasius, vol. 1. Auxentius the Cappadocian succeeded Dionysius. So Sigonius is right that in his place Auxentius was appointed bishop, for the thing itself cries out that something is missing. Auxentius is also mentioned in Jerome, letter 57, to Damasus.

units.la: Hilarius Vi&avorum episcopus] Hiero. in Chronico, Hila- rius episcopus Vi&avienfis factione Saturnini Arelatenfis episcopi, reliquorumque, qui cum eo erant, Arrianorum, ante triennium in Phrygiam pullos libros de nostra reli- gione componit.
units.tr: "Hilary, bishop of the Vitavi": Jerome in his Chronicle: Hilary, bishop of the Viennese, through the faction of Saturninus of Arles and the rest of the Arians who were with him, some three years earlier, while in exile in Phrygia, composed books on our religion.

units.la: Vi&avorum episcopus] ut, Vercellensium episcopus, Sic, Mediolanensium sacerdos: Arelatenfium episcopus. Mos loquendi Sulpicio familiaris.
units.tr: "Bishop of the Vitavi": as "bishop of the Vercellenses," and "priest of the Milanese," or "bishop of Arles." This way of speaking was familiar to Sulpicius.

units.la: Rhodanium quoque] in quibusdam editis, Rhodanum quoque, Similiter variant in hoc nomine codices Eufebiani. Nam pro Rhadianus, quod in editione Henrici Stephani, legendum arbitror Rhodanus: nisi quis malit Rhodianus. Apud Zozome- num legitur Podaνός, & in vita S. Athanafij Podavos.
units.tr: "Rhodanius also": in some printed editions it is "Rhodanum also." The manuscripts of Eusebius vary in the same way over this name. For "Rhadianus," which is in Henri Estienne's edition, I think one should read Rhodanus, unless someone prefers Rhodianus. In Zosimus it is read Podanos (Ποδανός), and in the Life of St Athanasius Podavos.

units.la: Et Dolanum antistitem] Sigonius reponit, & Hofium an- tiftitem. Sed tum dixisset potius, Rnodanium quoque & Hofium antistites. Ita mihi videtur. CL.V. Theodorus Cante- ris in litteris ad me datis suspicatur legendum, Rhodianu quo- que Tholofanum antistitem. De quo non dubitarem, fi scirem RhodaRhodanium ejus urbis episcopum fuisse. Idem submonuit me paullo post legendum videri, non cesserat Arrianus, in eo; parenthesin claudendam. Valde placet haec doctissimi viri conjectura.
units.tr: "And Dolanus the bishop": Sigonius substitutes "and Hosius the bishop." But then he would rather have said "Rhodanius also and Hosius, the bishops." So it seems to me. Theodorus Canterus, in letters sent to me, suspects one should read "Rhodianus also, the bishop of Toulouse," which I would not doubt, if I knew that Rhodanius had been bishop of that city. The same man advised me shortly afterwards that it seems to be read "the Arian had not yielded in this; the parenthesis should be closed. This learned man's conjecture greatly pleases me."

units.la: Pag 152. Abhinc annos quinque & quadraginta] hoc est anno Christi CCCLV. Omne enim tempus in Stiliconem consulem direxit, hoc est in annum Christi CCCC.
units.tr: p. 152. "Forty-five years ago": that is, in the year of Christ 355. For he extends all the time down to the consulship of Stilicho, that is, to the year of Christ 400.

units.la: Sed Liberius paullo post urbi reddítur ob seditiones Romanas] Hieronymus in Chronico, Romanae ecclesiae XXXIV ordinatur Liberius: quo in exilium ob fidem truso, omnes clerici juraverunt ut nullum alium suscipérent. Verùm cum Felix fuisset ab Arrianis in sacerdotium substitutus, plurimi pejeraverunt: & post annum cum Felice ejecti sunt, quia Liberius taedio victus exilij, & in haeretica pravitate subscribens, Romam quasi victor intraverat.
units.tr: "But Liberius was restored to the city shortly afterwards because of Roman seditions": Jerome in his Chronicle: In the thirty-fourth year of the Roman church Liberius is ordained; when he was driven into exile for the faith, all the clergy swore that they would receive no other. But when Felix had been set up by the Arians as bishop, many of them perjured themselves; and after a year they were cast out along with Felix, because Liberius, overcome by weariness of exile and subscribing to heretical depravity, had entered Rome as a victor.

units.la: Hominis veritatem] unitatem, Sigonius.
units.tr: "Truth of the man": Sigonius reads "unity."

units.la: Anomoeousiam] ἀνομοιούσιον [?]; unde ἀνομοιούσιος [?], dissimilis substantiae. Quod fortasse reponendum in Chronico Hieronymi ad annum Christi CCCLXVII. ubi vulgo, in qua omousion in omoeusion, eoque rejecto medio inter haec omoeusion Macedonianum dogma vindicaverunt. Editio nupera Scaligeri, in qua homousio anomoeoque rejecto, medium inter haec Homoeousion, &c. Quod ut non improbo, ita suspicor Hiero. potius scripsisse, in qua homousio anomoeousioque rejecto. Nam primum hoc propius accedit ad scripturam vulgatam: deinde anomoeon non ita exprimit dissimilitudinem substantiae. Docti viderint.
units.tr: "Anomoeousia": anomoeousion [ἀνομοιούσιον]; whence anomoeousios [ἀνομοιούσιος], of dissimilar substance. This perhaps should be restored in Jerome's Chronicle at the year of Christ 367, where the common text reads, "in which homoousion was changed into homoeousion, and so, with the middle term rejected, they claimed the Macedonian dogma for these homoeousion." Scaliger's recent edition reads, "in which homoousion and anomoeon were rejected, the middle between these, Homoeousion, etc." I do not disapprove of this, but I suspect Jerome rather wrote, "in which homoousion and anomoeousion were rejected." For first, this comes closer to the common text; second, anomoeon does not express dissimilarity of substance in this way. Learned men will judge.

units.la: Pag.153. Osium quoque ab Hispania] alij asserant Hosium scribentes: episcopus erat Cordubensis, sive, ut nostri loqui amant, Cordubensium.
units.tr: p. 153. "Hosius also from Spain": others assert the name is Hosius; he was bishop of Cordova, or, as we like to say, of the Cordubenses.

units.la: In eandem perfidiam concessisse opinio fuit] multorum, non omnium. Sane Augustinus innocentem Osium & catholicum contra haereticorum calumnias adstruit.
units.tr: "It was the opinion that he had given in to the same treachery": this was the opinion of many, not of all. Indeed Augustine maintains that Hosius was innocent and Catholic, against the slanders of the heretics.

units.la: Nicena synodus] in quo homousion decretum. Hosius autem, ut habetur in priore tomo Conciliorum, interroganti Constantio, utri rectius sentirent, qui Homousion an qui Homoeousion praedicarent, respondit, Utrosq; recte sentire. Quae sententia tam stulte prolata uno ab omnibus ore derisa & explosa est.
units.tr: "The Nicene synod": in which homoousion was decreed. Hosius, however, as is found in the first volume of the Councils, when Constantius asked him which of them more rightly thought, those who preached homoousion or those who preached homoeousion, replied that both thought rightly. This opinion, so foolishly put forward, was mocked and hissed down by everyone with one voice.

units.la: Nisi fatisceute aevo deliraverit] Isidorus de viris illustribus, Hosius post longum senium vetustatis accersitus a
units.tr: "Unless, his age failing, he had gone out of his mind": Isidore, On Illustrious Men: Hosius, after a long senility of old age, summoned by

units.la: Constantio, minisq; perterritus, metuens ne senex & di-ves damna rerum vel exilium paterétur, ilico Arrianæ impietati consensit.
units.tr: Constantius, and terrified by threats, fearing that as an old and wealthy man he would suffer the loss of his property or exile, at once consented to Arian impiety.

units.la: Fatiscente] deficiente. Sic epist. 3. nec fatiscentem causa-bor ætatem: & mox, fatiscentes[?] artus servire spiritui co-gebat: & Dialo. 1, segm. 5. corpus inedia fatiscebat, fides fir-ma durabat.
units.tr: "Failing": giving way. So in letter 3: "nor will I plead my failing age"; and soon: "his failing limbs compelled the body to serve the spirit." And in Dialogue 1, section 5: "the body was wasting away with hunger, but faith held firm."

units.la: Promisso eidem consulatu] quem post tamen adeptus est, licet rem effectui non tradiderit.
units.tr: "Having promised him the consulship": which he afterwards did obtain, though he did not bring the matter to effect.

units.la: Pag.154. Accitinumerative] lectio hæc a Galesinio est. Prius erat in libris acciti aut macti. Id Faber corrigit, inacti, quod interpretatur, coacti vel adacti, Semestrium lib. 3. cap. 12.
units.tr: p. 154. "Accitinumerative": this reading is Galesinus's. Earlier the books had "summoned" or "honoured." Faber corrects it to "compelled," which he explains as "forced or driven," Faber, Semestria, book 3, chapter 12.

units.la: Cellaria dare] dari mavult Sigonius, qui cellaria interpretatur hospitia sive cellas hospitales.
units.tr: "To give lodgings": Sigonius prefers "to be given," and explains the lodgings as hospitable rooms or cells.

units.la: Sed id nostris] i.catholicis. Quæ sequuntur, id est Aquitanis, Gallis ac Britannis, aglossemate redundant. Vide Sigonium.
units.tr: "But this was to our people": that is, to the Catholics. What follows, that is, "the Aquitanians, Gauls and Britons," is a superfluous gloss. See Sigonius.

units.la: Ita in utriusque] probo. ita in utreisque, nisi mavelis vitæ in utreisq. Hoc est tam in iis qui expublice[?] alebantur quam in iis qui ex proprio vivebant. Vide Fabrum loco superius citato. Nam ab eo hæc habeo.
units.tr: "So in the case of each": I approve. "So in each of the two" (ita in utreisque), unless you prefer "of life in each" (vitae in utrisque). That is, as much among those who were supported at public expense as among those who lived on their own means. See Faber at the place cited above, for I have these points from him.

units.la: Edentum de industria vacantem] non omnino displicet Gi-felini illud, ædem tum, ut sig. eos ædem quandam tunc vacan-tem orationis loco cepisse. Sed quæramus amplius.
units.tr: "Deliberately leaving the temple empty": Gifelinus's suggestion, that they then took some temple which was then empty in place of a speech, is not wholly displeasing. But let us look further.

units.la: Pag.155. Placuit decem legatos mitti] Chronicon Hiero. Synodus apud Ariminū & Seleuciam Isauriæ facta, in qua antiqua patrum fides decem numero legatorum, debinc omnium, proditione damnata est.
units.tr: p. 155. "It was decided to send ten envoys": Jerome's Chronicle: the synod held at Ariminum and at Seleucia in Isauria, in which the ancient faith of the Fathers was condemned by treachery, first by a number of ten envoys, then by all.

units.la: Evectionis copia] Sic lib. 12. cod. de cursu publ. evectionū copiā Senatui, cū proficiscēdi ad nos necesitas fuerit, Serenitas nostra largita est, i.libellū publicū tuti aliberi itineris.
units.tr: "Supply of transport (evectionis copia)": so in book 12 of the Code, On the public post: "Our Serenity has granted the Senate a supply of transport, whenever necessity requires them to set out to us," that is, a public letter granting safe and free passage.

units.la: Pag. 156. Volentes miscere] Sigonius emendat volentem, & Gifelinus, miscuere. Idem volentes opponit episcopis compul-sis & coactis concilio adesse.
units.tr: p. 156. "Wishing to mix": Sigonius emends it to "wishing" in the singular, and Gifelinus to "they mixed." The same "wishing" is set against bishops compelled and forced to attend the council.

units.la: Georgius ab Alexandria] id est, Alexandrinus episcopus & Constantio constitutus, cum prius fuisset episcopus Laodicenus. Alii sive Acacius Cæsariensis episcopus Eudoxius Germanicia, discipulus Ætij: Vranius Tyri episcopus.
units.tr: "George from Alexandria": that is, the bishop of Alexandria, appointed by Constantius, although previously he had been bishop of Laodicea. Others: Acacius, bishop of Caesarea; Eudoxius of Germanicia, a pupil of Aetius; Uranius, bishop of Tyre.

units.la: Leontius] Leontinus. Galesinus.
units.tr: "Leontius": Galesinus reads "Leontinus."

units.la: Theodolus] in Athanasio Theodulus, id est, servus Dei. Pag.
units.tr: "Theodolus": in Athanasius it is "Theodulus," that is, servant of God. p.

units.la: Tribus libellis publice datis] non tres, sed unum librum nominat Hiero, qui hoc accidisse scribit anno Christi CCCLXIV. Hilarius, inquit, cum apud Constantinopolim librum prose Constantio porrexisset, ad Gallias rediit.
units.tr: "Three little books publicly given": Jerome names not three but one book, and he writes that this happened in the year of Christ 364: "Hilary, when he had presented one book to Constantius at Constantinople, returned to Gaul."

units.la: Paulinus Treverorum episcopus in Phrygia exulans moritur an. Christi CCCLIX.
units.tr: Paulinus, bishop of Trier, dies in exile in Phrygia in the year of Christ 359.

units.la: In patria Pictavii mortuus est, Valentiniano ac Valente imperatibus, anno Christi CCCLXVII (Hiero nunc sequor) qui a reditu ipsius erat septimus. Nā rediit ann. Christi CCCLXI, sed expende. Nam exemplaria Hiero. in annis non consentiunt.
units.tr: He died in his homeland of Poitiers, in the reign of Valentinian and Valens, in the year of Christ 367 (I follow Jerome here), which was the seventh year after his return. For he returned in the year of Christ 361, but weigh this. For the copies of Jerome do not agree on the years.

units.la: Prosper in Chronico, Ea tempestate Priscillianus episcopus de Galliæcia, ex Manichæorum & Gnosticorum dogmate haeresin nominis sui condidit. Quippe docebat animam esse ex propria Dei substantia. Hiero. epist. 82, quæ opinio & Manichæi fuit & Stoicorum. Idem ibid.
units.tr: Prosper in his Chronicle: At that time Priscillian, bishop from Galicia, founded a heresy under his own name from the doctrine of the Manichaeans and Gnostics. For he taught that the soul is from the very substance of God; this opinion belonged to both the Manichaeans and the Stoics. Idem, ibid.

units.la: Agape quædam] Hiero. In Hispania Agape Elpidium, mulierem virum, cœcū cœca duxit in foveam, lucceflorem quoque Priscillianum habuit, Zoroastrem magi studiosissimum.
units.tr: "A certain Agape": Jerome: In Spain Agape led Elpidius, an effeminate man, a blind man blind into a pit; she also had Priscillian as her follower, a most devoted student of Zoroaster the magus.

units.la: Quin & magicas artes, &c. nihil mirum cum eum Marcus, qui hanc hæresin primus in Hispaniam intulit, ar-tem magicæ scientissimus fuerit. Quem Isidorus Maxim d'scipulum & Priscilliani magistrum vocat.
units.tr: "Also magic arts, etc.": nothing is surprising, since Marcus, who first brought this heresy into Spain, was most skilled in the art of magic. Isidore calls him a disciple of Maximus and the teacher of Priscillian.

units.la: Emeritæ ætatis] aßentior iis qui legunt, Emeritæ civitatis. Augusta Emerita civitas Lusitaniæ, quæ Ptolemæo ἡμέτερα, ab Augusti militibus emeritis sic appellata creditur.
units.tr: "Of veteran age": I agree with those who read "of the veteran city." Augusta Emerita, a city of Lusitania, which Ptolemy calls by a name meaning "ours," is believed to have been so named from Augustus's veteran soldiers.

units.la: Elusanam plebem] nihil mutandum. Elusfo opidum in finibus Nitiobrigum, quæ amni Draguio a Petrocoriis dividuntur. Vulgo Laufun.
units.tr: "The common people of Elusa": nothing needs changing. Elusa is a town in the territory of the Nitiobriges, who are divided from the Petrocorii by the river Draguius; commonly called Laufun.

units.la: Pag. 166. In quis erat Euchrocia & filia ejus Procula. Euchrocia sive Euchrotia uxor erat Delphidij rhetoris, quem Ausonius recenset inter Burdigalenses professores. Idem Euchrociam cum filia Procula significat, cum ait, Delphidium alloquens, Minus malorum munere expertus Dei Medio quod aevi raptus es, Errore quod non deviantis filiae, Poenaque laesus conjugi[?]n.
units.tr: Page 166. In which were Euchrocia and her daughter Procula. Euchrocia, or Euchrotia, was the wife of Delphidius the rhetorician, whom Ausonius lists among the teachers of Bordeaux. The same poet means Euchrocia together with her daughter Procula when, addressing Delphidius, he says: "You were snatched away in the middle of your life by God's gift of lesser evils, not through the error of a daughter who did not go astray, and, wounded by punishment, [you were taken from] your wife."

units.la: Cum magistro officiorum] non displicet conjectura Sigonij, qui legendum putat, tum magistro officiorum, ut Macedonium intelligatur eo tempore magister officiorum.
units.tr: With the master of the offices] Sigonius's conjecture is not unwelcome, who thinks it should be read "then with the master of the offices," so that Macedonius is understood to have been master of the offices at that time.

units.la: Trachio] sententia postulat ut reponatur Idacio. Idem.
units.tr: Trachio] The sense requires that Idacio be restored. The same.

units.la: Pag. 167. Hispaniarum vicario] hic abesse deferatur, aut aliquid tale.
units.tr: Page 167. Vicar of the Spains] Here something should be understood as missing, or something of the kind.

units.la: Pag. 168. Idacius & Ithacius] pro Idacius legitur Hylatius in Hiero. de viris illustribus. Sed est qui pro eo reponat Vrsatius: Nam Isidorus, Sigebertus Gemblacensis & Hermannus Contra-ctus scribunt Vrsatium cum Ithacio propter accusationem Priscil-liani communione ecclesiae privatum & exilio damnatum. Vide sequentia.
units.tr: Page 168. Idacius and Ithacius] In Jerome's On Illustrious Men Hylatius is read instead of Idacius. But some would substitute Ursatius for him: for Isidore, Sigebert of Gembloux and Hermann Contractus write that Ursatius, together with Ithacius on account of the accusation of Priscillian, was deprived of communion with the Church and condemned to exile. See what follows.

units.la: Permissum q; id nostrorum inconstantia] causa erat ecclesiastica, ac proinde pertinebat ad sacerdotes, non ad ipsum imperatorem. Sed ea aetate ipsi sacerdotes adulabantur principibus, quo factum ut multi indigna sacerdotali dignitate commiserint. Cum ad Maximum, inquit hic noster in vita Martini, ferocis ingenij virum & bellorum civilium victoria elatum, plures ex diversis partibus episcopi convenissent, & foeda circa Principem adulatio notaretur, seq; degeneri inconstantia regiae clientelae sacerdotalis dignitas subdidisset, in solo Martino apostolica autoritas permanebat. Haec ibi Sulpicius, cap. 23.
units.tr: "And this was permitted through the inconstancy of our people" The cause was ecclesiastical, and therefore belonged to the bishops, not to the emperor himself. But in that age the bishops themselves flattered the princes, with the result that many committed things unworthy of their episcopal dignity. When the bishops from various regions, says our author in the Life of Martin, had gathered before Maximus, a man of fierce temper and elated by victory in civil wars, and a shameful flattery of the prince was noticed, and the dignity of the priesthood, through a base inconstancy, had been made subject to the royal clientage, apostolic authority remained in Martin alone. So Sulpicius there, chapter 23.

units.la: Pag. 169. Martino episcopo] Turonensi, cujus etiam vitam & miracula descripsit, ubi eum summum sacerdotem appellat. Sic in Iobasin Augustinus vocatur הכהן הגדול[?], id est, sacerdos magnus.
units.tr: Page 169. Bishop Martin] of Tours, whose life and miracles he also wrote, where he calls him the chief priest. So in Iobasin Augustine is called הכהן הגדול [the high priest], that is, the great priest.

units.la: Apostolis conferendo] mirum ni scripsit, conferendo. Sic epist. 2. de hoc eodem Martino, ut est conlertus Apostolis & Prophetis.
units.tr: Conferring on the apostles] It would be surprising if he had not written "conferendo." So in his second letter about this same Martin, "as he is compared with the apostles and prophets."

units.la: Et Rufum] quaerendum an is sit qui post episcopatu dejectus fuit quod pseudoprophetam quendam, qui se Eliam fingebat, in Hispaniis adorasset, ejus mentio in vita Martini, pag. 214.
units.tr: And Rufus] It must be inquired whether he is the one who, after being deposed from the episcopate, worshipped in Spain a certain pseudo-prophet who pretended to be Elijah. His mention is in the Life of Martin, page 214.

units.la: Præfecto Evodio] præfectus erat prætorio Maximi, idemq; consul, vir quo nihil unquam justius, inquit Sulpicius noster in vita Martini, cap. 23.
units.tr: Prefect Evodius] He was praetorian prefect under Maximus, and also consul, a man than whom nothing was ever more just, says our Sulpicius in the Life of Martin, chapter 23.

units.la: Pag 170. Feiicissimus & Armenius] Hiero. addit Iulia-num quendam.
units.tr: Page 170. Felicissimus and Armenius] Jerome adds a certain Julianus.

units.la: Latronianus] sic Prosper Aquitanus in Chronico suo. Alij Matronianum vocant, quem dicunt fuisse virum eruditum & in opere metrico veteribus comparandum. Vide Hiero. de viris illustribus & Chronicon Vasei.
units.tr: Latronianus] So Prosper of Aquitaine in his Chronicle. Others call him Matronianus, whom they say was a learned man and comparable to the ancients in metrical composition. See Jerome's On Illustrious Men and the Chronicle of Vasaeus.

units.la: In Sylinam insulam] non una, sed plures insulæ sunt, quas nunc Belgici Sorlingas, antiqui Græci Hesperidas & Cassiteri-das vocant. Vide sis Britanniam Cambdeni, pag. 714.
units.tr: Into the island of Sylina] There is not one island but several, which the Belgians now call the Sorlingas and the ancient Greeks the Hesperides and Cassiterides. See also Camden's Britannia, page 714.

units.la: Tyberianus] scribo Iberianus. Erat autem Baeticus. Vide Hiero in Tiberiano.
units.tr: Tyberianus] I write Iberianus. He was a Baetican. See Jerome on Tiberianus.

units.la: Pag.171. Egregio publico] id est, bono & emolumento publico. Tacitus ita locutus est Annal. lib. 3.
units.tr: Page 171. Egregio publico] that is, for the good and advantage of the public. Tacitus spoke thus in Annals book 3.

units.la: Solus tamen omnium episcopatu detrusus] Theognistus quidam non Ithacium modo, sed omnes episcopos, qui Ithacio communicantes communem sibi caussam fecerant, solus lata sententia condemnaverat. Dial. 3. segm. 15.
units.tr: Yet he alone of all was thrust down from the episcopate] A certain Theognistus had condemned by sentence not only Ithacius but all the bishops who had communicated with Ithacius and made his cause their own. Dialogue 3, section 15.

units.la: Nardacius] Prosper Aquitanus in Chronico, Timasio & Promoto conff. Ithacius & Nardacius Ecclesiæ communione privantur: ubi tamen legendum ex editione nupera, & alia Parisiensi, qua domi utor, Ithacius & Ursatius. Sic etiam Isidorus, Sigebertus autor, propterea communione privatos, quod episcopi nefas esse ducerent, cujuscunque modi hominem episcoporum accusatione necari. Ceterum Ithacius iste librum sub apologetici specie edidit, in quo detestanda Priscilliani dogmata & maleficiorum artes, & libidinum probra demonstravit.
units.tr: Nardacius] Prosper of Aquitaine in the Chronicle, under the consuls Timasius and Promotus: "Ithacius and Nardacius are deprived of communion with the Church." But there one should read, according to the recent edition and another Parisian one that I use at home, "Ithacius and Ursatius." So too Isidore and Sigebert the author, on the ground that the bishops thought it wrong for any man of whatever kind to be put to death through an accusation by bishops. Moreover, that Ithacius published a book under the guise of an apology, in which he exposed the detestable doctrines of Priscillian, his magical arts and his shameful lusts.

units.la: Postea ut martyrem colere coeperunt] Petrus de Natalibus, ut habetur in Chronico Hispaniæ, Priscillianum & Matronianum in sanctorum martyrum catalogum cooptavit. Quod Hieronymi auctoritate confirmare dum voluit, né ille palam offendit se in ejus viri libris plane hospitem esse.
units.tr: Afterwards they began to honour him as a martyr] Peter de Natalibus, as found in the Chronicle of Spain, enrolled Priscillian and Matronianus in the catalogue of holy martyrs. In trying to confirm this by the authority of Jerome, he was afraid lest it openly appear that he was entirely a stranger to that man's books.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: Voces et phrases aliquot peculiares ex historia sacra Sulp. Severi.
units.tr: Some peculiar words and phrases from the sacred history of Sulpicius Severus.

units.la: ÆGypto advenerat, pag.20.
units.tr: Aegypto advenerat (had arrived in Egypt), p. 20.

units.la: Anni sex millia, 4.
units.tr: Anni sex millia (six thousand years), 4.

units.la: Altarium, 30.
units.tr: Altarium (of altars), 30.

units.la: Chaldæi pro Magis aut Mathematicis
units.tr: Chaldaei for Magi or mathematicians.
23 (twice), 43 and 44.

units.la: Conjugia, uxores, 67.
units.tr: Conjugia, uxores (marriages, wives), 67.

units.la: Pag. 14. lin. 4. dediße. 18. 1. leg. 1. legendum. 74. 1. neque recte Sigonius. 84. 17. quicquid inter Monios, & Porro, penitus delendum. 89. 1. [illegible, ~6 letters]. 113. 31. praei, malim eis. 115. 10. Servamve. 138. ἐξεικονισμα[?]. 131. 22. Vilonathan. 140. 7. repono III M aut MMM 24. Baalim. 144. 18. varietas. 166. 14. perinaciter. 167. 6. adde, Eusebius hoc diceret, Hebraeorum Israel 168. 21. Quia habuisti. 170. 8. ὑοτεβὴς[?]. 182. 32. σαρξ[?] τῆς. 183. 21. est a Nisan. 189. 26. reliquos fecerat. 208. 7. sæpe. 229. 16. Oviæ. 251. 6. Het-culianos. 269. 2. dediße. 270. 2. vel, Pretogoricas.
units.tr: Page 14, line 4: "dediße" (to have given). Page 18, line 1: for "leg." read "legendum" (to be read). Page 74, line 1: "neque recte Sigonius" (nor did Sigonius rightly). Page 84, line 17: whatever lies between "Monios" and "Porro" is to be deleted entirely. Page 89, line 1: [illegible, about six letters]. Page 113, line 31: "praei"; I would prefer "eis" (to them). Page 115, line 10: "Servamve" (and whether I saved). Page 138: "ἐξεικονισμα[?]" (exeikonisma). Page 131, line 22: "Vilonathan". Page 140, line 7: I would substitute "III M" or "MMM" (3,000 or 3,000,000) for "24"; "Baalim". Page 144, line 18: "varietas" (variety). Page 166, line 14: "perinaciter" (obstinately). Page 167, line 6: add "Eusebius said this", "Hebraeorum Israel" (of the Hebrews, Israel). Page 168, line 21: "Quia habuisti" (because you had). Page 170, line 8: "ὑοτεβὴς[?]" (hypotebes[?]). Page 182, line 32: "σαρξ[?] τῆς" (sarx[?] tes, flesh of the). Page 183, line 21: "est a Nisan" (is from Nisan). Page 189, line 26: "reliquos fecerat" (he had made the rest). Page 208, line 7: "sæpe" (often). Page 229, line 16: "Oviæ". Page 251, line 6: "Het-culianos". Page 269, line 2: "dediße" (to have given). Page 270, line 2: for "vel" read "Pretogoricas".
